title: perf: log-mel FFT twiddle precompute + alloc-elimination (mel frontend)
description: whisper.cpp's recursive fft (src/native_engine/mel.rs) recomputes cos/sin twiddles per butterfly per frame; the odd-N base case dft(25) is reached 16x/frame x 3000 frames, ~60M f64 transcendentals per 30s audio. L1 (this turn): precompute level + DFT twiddle tables once (cached OnceLock, shared across mel worker threads), bit-exact (same f64 math + as-f32 narrowing at build time). Guarded by fft_twiddle_table_is_bit_exact_vs_inline_reference (10 widths x 64 seeds). L2 (follow-up): eliminate the per-call Vec allocations in the recursive fft (even/odd/even_fft/odd_fft, ~60 allocs/frame) via per-thread scratch buffers. Measured head-to-head via native_engine/mel/mel_30s vs mel-pre baseline (269ms).
notes: L1 LANDED in commit 656f55c (origin/main + master): log-mel FFT twiddle precompute. Measured native_engine/mel/mel_30s 269.06ms -> 29.23ms (-89.1%, p=0.00, ~9.2x) same-worker A/B on vmi1149989. Bit-exact: standalone parity 418800 outputs / 0 mismatches + in-tree test fft_twiddle_table_is_bit_exact_vs_inline_reference. L2 (per-call alloc elimination in recursive fft via per-thread scratch) remains open as follow-up. Ledger: docs/PERF_LEDGER.md.
close_reason: L1 shipped (9.2x mel); L2 measured (1.21x FFT, ~0 e2e) and deferred per revert-~0-gain.

title: Build original-vs-franken benchmark ledger harness
description:
## Background
The mission is to dominate the original OpenAI Whisper / whisper.cpp stack on realistic workloads, but current artifacts mix true original-vs-franken proof with internal franken policy comparisons. This bead establishes the head-to-head measurement substrate and makes docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md the claim ledger.

## Scope
Create a reproducible per-crate benchmark/evidence harness that records every original-vs-franken win, loss, neutral result, and reverted candidate. The harness must run only this crate, with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/franken_whisper-cod-a` and `rch exec -- cargo bench --release ...`; never run workspace-wide benches.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparators: `whisper.cpp` / `whisper-cli` CPU for primary CPU claims; optional GPU comparator as a clearly labeled control. OpenAI Whisper Python and related original-stack tools can be added only when the workload needs that comparator.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- `alien_cs_graveyard.md` section 0.10 statistical benchmarking standard.
- `alien_cs_graveyard.md` section 0.19 evidence ledger schema.
- `profiling-software-performance`: fingerprint, p50/p95/p99, RSS, hotspot table.
- `extreme-software-optimization`: one lever, isomorphism proof, re-profile.

## Validation
Artifacts for each run must include env/fingerprint, exact command lines, raw criterion or hyperfine output, p50/p95/p99, RSS/user CPU when available, conformance/golden hashes, and a ledger row in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md or its successor.

## Tests
Run the smallest relevant per-crate Criterion bench through rch after harness changes, plus `cargo fmt --check` if code changes. No claim may be accepted from a single run or from cross-host-only evidence.

## Success Criteria
A future agent can add a new measured claim by following one documented command block and gets a machine-readable ratio row: workload, franken path, original path, speed_ratio, conformance status, artifact path, and verdict.

Rejected as product-speed lever; evidence recorded in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

title: Measure and fix shipped release-profile native speed gap
description:
## Background
Existing artifacts say the distribution `release` profile uses `opt-level = \"z\"` and was about 26% slower than `release-perf` on `large-v3-turbo`. The README headline claims are from `release-perf`, but users run shipped release binaries. If shipped release loses to whisper.cpp while release-perf is at parity, this is the biggest real-world domination gap.

## Scope
Measure native `release`, native `release-perf`, and original `whisper.cpp` CPU on the same host and same audio/model corpus. If the release profile is a confirmed top lever, make one Cargo profile change only, then re-benchmark and update the ledger. Do not combine with native-engine kernel changes.

## Baseline Comparator
Primary: `whisper.cpp` CPU on the same input/model. Controls: native `release-perf`; optional `whisper.cpp` GPU/Metal clearly marked as a hardware-control loss/win, not a CPU claim.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard section 0.10: statistical benchmark acceptance, p50/p95/p99 and confidence interval discipline.
- Extreme optimization: one profile lever per commit; prove behavior unchanged via golden transcripts and conformance hashes.
- Artifact coding: policy decision is not adaptive; fallback is reverting the Cargo profile if binary size or wall time fails budget.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: bigger binaries or slower cold builds. Budgeted mode: record binary size, build time, wall, user CPU, and conformance. Fallback trigger: less than 3% wall win vs current release or unacceptable binary-size growth per release owner policy.

## Validation
Run per-crate through rch only, with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/franken_whisper-cod-a`. Required gates: original-vs-franken ratio row, golden transcript hash match, conformance green, and no new negative-evidence collision.

## Success Criteria
Shipped release binary is at least parity with current release-perf against whisper.cpp CPU on `tiny.en` and `large-v3-turbo`, or the bead closes as negative evidence with exact ratio and reason.
close_reason: Completed: release profile opt-level=3 is already landed on main in 866760c with docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md release-profile ratio evidence; current Cargo.toml keeps [profile.release] opt-level=3.

title: Foundation: Legacy Analysis, Project Infrastructure, and Porting Strategy
description:
EPIC: Foundation & Legacy Analysis

This epic covers the foundational work that ALL other work depends on. franken_whisper is a Rust-native ASR system that merges the best IDEAS (not code) from three legacy projects into something radically better:

- legacy_whispercpp (C/C++): Fast local inference, VAD (Silero), streaming, multi-platform HW accel, TinyDiarize, word-level timestamps, quantized models, 60+ CLI flags
- legacy_insanely_fast_whisper (Python): Flash Attention 2 (15x speedup), GPU batching, ergonomic CLI, pyannote diarization
- legacy_whisper_diarization (Python): Multi-stage pipeline (Demucs source separation → Faster-Whisper → CTC forced alignment → NeMo TitaNet speaker embeddings → multilingual punctuation restoration)

The merger pattern follows frankentui's proven methodology: SYNTHESIS not merger, CONCEPTS not copy-paste, DESIGN-DRIVEN not code-driven. The frankentui project demonstrated that planning before code (the first 48 hours were ALL planning) produces dramatically better results.

This project must deeply integrate with:
- asupersync: Cancel-correct async orchestration (not just Runtime::new — use Cx, regions, finalizers, budgets)
- frankensqlite: MVCC concurrent writes + RaptorQ durability (not just basic open/execute)
- frankentorch: GPU tensor operations + autograd (for acceleration beyond simple softmax)
- frankenjax: JIT-compiled transform graphs (for declarative computation paths)
- frankentui: Optional TUI for human operators

The project is BOTH a reusable Rust library AND a standalone CLI with robot mode (agent-first NDJSON) + optional TUI.

Key constraints: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], Rust 2024 edition, nightly toolchain, Cargo only, fsqlite only (no rusqlite).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All three legacy projects (whisper.cpp, insanely-fast-whisper, whisper-diarization) analyzed with strengths/weaknesses documented
- Cargo.toml validates with correct edition, features, dependencies
- All quality gates pass (fmt, check, clippy, test)
- FEATURE_PARITY.md tracks every legacy feature with migration status
- PROPOSED_ARCHITECTURE.md reflects deep integration plan
- Porting strategy document is self-contained and actionable.
acceptance_criteria: - All three legacy projects (whisper.cpp, insanely-fast-whisper, whisper-diarization) analyzed with strengths/weaknesses documented. - Cargo.toml validates with correct edition, features, dependencies. - All quality gates pass (fmt, check, clippy, test). - FEATURE_PARITY.md tracks every legacy feature with migration status. - PROPOSED_ARCHITECTURE.md reflects deep integration plan. - Porting strategy document is self-contained and actionable.

title: Document legacy project analysis: what each project excels at
description:

FROM legacy_whispercpp (C/C++):

- Multi-platform HW acceleration: ARM NEON, AVX/AVX2, Metal, Core ML, CUDA/cuBLAS, Vulkan, OpenVINO

- BetterTransformer integration
- FP16 mixed precision
- Distil-whisper support for smaller model footprint
- Clean ergonomic CLI design (simple, opinionated)
- Direct URL input support (download and transcribe)
- Rich progress indicators

title: native_engine/mel.rs: log-mel frontend (mixed-radix FFT, exact whisper semantics)
description:
Implement src/native_engine/mel.rs: log-mel spectrogram frontend (pure Rust, exact whisper semantics).

SPEC (mirror whisper.cpp log_mel_spectrogram):
- Constants: SAMPLE_RATE 16000, N_FFT 400, HOP 160, CHUNK 30s -> 3000 mel frames per window; n_mel from model (80 or 128).
- Hann window (periodic, length 400): w[i] = 0.5*(1 - cos(2*pi*i/400)).
- Reflective padding of N_FFT/2 on both sides (whisper.cpp pads with reflection); audio windows beyond end zero-padded to full 30s chunk (3000 frames) — match whisper.cpp behavior of padding to chunk.
- FFT: iterative radix-2 complex FFT, length 400 is NOT a power of two — whisper.cpp zero-pads?? NO: whisper.cpp uses a hybrid (dft for non-pow2). DECISION: implement Bluestein or mixed-radix? SIMPLEST CORRECT: real-input DFT length-400 via Goertzel is O(N^2)=160k ops/frame * 3000 frames = 480M flops — too slow in debug but fine in release w/ rayon? Better: radix-2 FFT of length 512 is WRONG (changes bins). Use mixed-radix FFT supporting 400 = 2^4 * 5^2 (radix-2 + radix-5 stages), or Bluestein via pow2 1024. Implement radix-2+radix-5 mixed FFT with tests vs naive DFT (exact within 1e-4). Power spectrum bins 0..=200 (onesided 201).
- Mel projection: filters (n_mel x 201) from ggml file (A1) matmul power spectrum -> mel energies; log10(max(e,1e-10)); dynamic-range clamp: log_spec = max(log_spec, log_spec.max() - 8.0); normalize (log_spec + 4.0)/4.0. EXACTLY as whisper.cpp/openai.
- Parallelize frames with rayon (via ft-kernel-cpu's rayon — or std::thread::scope chunks; keep it simple, frames are independent).
- API: fn log_mel(samples: &[f32], filters: &MelFilterbank, n_threads) -> Mel { n_mel, n_frames, data } and helper to slice/pad a 30s window -> 3000 frames.
TESTS: (1) FFT vs naive DFT on random vectors (sizes 400, 200) rel err < 1e-4; (2) Parseval energy check; (3) golden test: silence -> all frames equal floor value (compute expected analytically); (4) 440Hz sine -> argmax mel bin matches analytic mel bin for 440Hz given the real tiny.en filterbank (gated on model presence); (5) determinism across thread counts.
close_reason: Implemented log-mel frontend in src/native_engine/mel.rs: periodic Hann window, exact whisper.cpp padding (leading reflective N_FFT/2, trailing 30s+N_FFT/2 zeros), recursive radix-2 FFT with naive-DFT odd base case (400->200->100->50->25), power spectrum re^2+im^2, 201-bin mel projection, log10(1e-10) floor, global max-8 clamp, (x+4)/4 normalize. std::thread::scope frame parallelism (no rayon). 6 tests pass incl FFT-vs-naive-DFT (400/256/200/5 <1e-4), Parseval, silence->-1.5 floor, n_threads 1==4 determinism, chunk_frames silence-floor padding, gated 440Hz argmax. clippy/rustfmt clean, no unsafe, no unwrap outside tests.

- Non-diarization: whisper_cpp → insanely_fast → whisper_diarization

title: Implement unified output format normalization across all backends

title: Robot Mode: Agent-First NDJSON Interface Enhancement
description:
EPIC: Robot Mode Enhancement

Robot mode is the agent-first interface — line-oriented NDJSON events streamed in real-time. This is how other programs (AI agents, automation scripts, CI/CD) interact with franken_whisper. It MUST be:
- Stable schema (versioned, backward-compatible)
- Deterministic where possible
- Explicit error codes (enumerated, documented)
- Line-oriented (jsonl/ndjson)
- Easy to pipe into other tools

Current implementation is functional but can be enhanced:
1. Schema versioning: Include schema_version in every event so consumers can adapt
2. Error code enumeration: Replace ad-hoc error strings with structured codes
3. Progress estimation: Include estimated_progress_pct in stage events
4. Streaming partial transcripts: Emit partial transcript text as segments are produced (not just at completion)
5. Backend availability query: `robot backends` command to list available backends with capabilities
6. Run comparison: `robot diff <run1> <run2>` to compare transcription results
7. Health check: `robot health` to verify system readiness
8. Input validation: `robot validate --input <file>` to check input before committing to a run

The event schema should be documented as a JSON Schema artifact that can be consumed by typed language generators.

Key files: src/robot.rs (112 lines), src/main.rs (robot command handling)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Robot mode outputs stable, versioned NDJSON schema
- All events have explicit error codes
- Schema versioning supports backward compatibility
- Event ordering is guaranteed monotonic
- All robot mode contract tests pass.

title: JSONL Sync: Enhanced Export/Import with Incremental Sync
description:
EPIC: JSONL Sync Enhancement

The JSONL sync system provides one-way export/import between SQLite and JSONL files. This serves auditability (git-friendly), backup, and cross-device transfer.

Current implementation (~900 lines) includes:
- Atomic export with manifest (schema version, timestamps, row counts, SHA256 checksums)
- Import with conflict policies (reject or overwrite)
- File-based locking (PID + timestamp, 5-minute stale detection)
- Sync conflict logging

Enhancement goals:
1. Incremental export: Only export records changed since last export (using updated_at timestamps or WAL position)
2. Selective export: Export specific runs, date ranges, or backends
3. Cross-device merge protocol: More sophisticated conflict resolution (3-way merge using common ancestor)
4. Compression: gzip/zstd compressed JSONL for large datasets
5. Streaming import: Process JSONL line-by-line instead of loading entire file
6. Sync telemetry: Report sync statistics (rows synced, conflicts, duration) as robot events
7. JSONL validation: `sync validate` command to verify JSONL integrity without importing

The sync system follows the project's SQLite+JSONL contract: SQLite is source of truth, JSONL is for auditability and recovery. One-way sync at a time, locked and atomic.

Key files: src/sync.rs (~900 lines)
Related docs: SYNC_STRATEGY.md, RECOVERY_RUNBOOK.md

## Acceptance Criteria
- JSONL export produces complete, checksummed snapshots
- JSONL import handles all conflict policies (reject, skip, overwrite)
- Locking prevents concurrent export/import corruption
- Round-trip: export then import produces identical DB state
- All sync tests pass.

title: EPIC: YouTube ingestion pipeline (yt-dlp orchestration -> native transcription -> md+json)
description:
GOAL: `franken_whisper youtube` — ingest YouTube video URLs (repeated --url), a batch file (one URL/line, #-comments), or playlist URLs; download audio via yt-dlp (orchestrated external tool, probed like whisper-cli/ffmpeg); transcribe with the native engine; emit per-video markdown (call-transcript style: title header, metadata block, timestamped paragraphs with youtu.be deep links, SPEAKER_NN when diarized) + JSON (video metadata + per-utterance records with confidence/window stats).

DESIGN (settled 2026-06-06 from /tmp archaeology of yt-dlp + bulk_youtube_transcript_optimizer):
- yt-dlp CLI contract (integration cheat-sheet, agent-verified): expand = `--flat-playlist --dump-json`; metadata = `-j --no-simulate`; download = `-f ba --no-playlist -o TEMPLATE --print after_move:filepath` + politeness `--sleep-interval 2 --max-sleep-interval 5 --retries 10`; batch = read file ourselves (we need per-URL state, not yt-dlp's batch mode); exit codes 0/1/2/101; probe `--version`, warn if >90 days old. Download bestaudio AS-IS (no -x re-encode) — franken_whisper's own normalize stage handles 16k mono.
- Naming: dual-filename convention (optimizer harvest): sanitized `{upload_date} - {title} [{id}]` base, video id as stable suffix; ASCII-safe sanitizer, length-trimmed; original title preserved in JSON.
- Layout: <out_dir>/audio/<base>.<ext>, <out_dir>/<base>.md, <out_dir>/<base>.json, <out_dir>/.fw_youtube_manifest.json (per-video state machine: pending|expanding|downloading|transcribing|rendering|done|failed{error} — idempotent resume: done videos skipped, failed retried unless --no-retry).

title: youtube: robot-mode NDJSON per-video events
description:
The `youtube` subcommand currently emits only a human one-line summary (or a single final JSON blob with `--json-summary`). The rest of franken_whisper exposes a robot interface (`robot run`, etc.) that streams sequenced, timestamped NDJSON stage events on schema `1.0.0`. The youtube path should offer a matching robot sub-mode that streams per-video stage events instead of a single terminal summary.

Proposed contract (NDJSON, one object per line, stable schema):
- `youtube.run_start` — request accepted; echoes resolved options (output_dir, concurrency, backend, diarize).
- `youtube.discovered` — per video, once resolution/playlist expansion yields it: {id, title, url, playlist_id?}.
- `youtube.downloading` / `youtube.downloaded` — per video, around the yt-dlp fetch: {id, audio_path?, bytes?}.
- `youtube.transcribing` / `youtube.done` — per video, around transcription: {id, md_path, json_path, wall_ms?, rtf?} on done.
- `youtube.skipped` — per video already `done` in the manifest: {id, reason:"already_done"}.
- `youtube.failed` — per video failure: {id, title, error, attempts}.
- `youtube.run_complete` — terminal aggregate: {done:[], skipped:[], failed:[], cancelled:bool}.

Notes:
- Each event carries `schema_version`, a monotonic `seq`, and an RFC-3339 `ts`, matching the existing robot stage-event envelope.
- Honor cancellation: on Ctrl+C emit `youtube.failed`/no further events and a `youtube.run_complete` with `cancelled:true`.
- Could be surfaced as `franken_whisper robot youtube ...` or a `--robot` flag on `youtube`; pick whichever matches the existing robot-interface convention.
- The current `--json-summary` (single final blob) stays as the lightweight scripting path; this adds the streaming path.

title: TTY Audio: Low-Bandwidth Audio Relay and Streaming
description:
EPIC: TTY Audio Enhancement

The TTY audio system is a unique innovation — sending audio over terminal PTY/SSH channels where binary streaming is awkward. Current implementation: μ-law encoding + zlib compression + base64 + NDJSON frames.

This is genuinely novel. No legacy project has anything like it. Enhancement goals:
1. Adaptive bitrate: Detect available bandwidth and adjust chunk size/compression
2. Real-time streaming: Currently only file encode/decode; add live mic → NDJSON → remote decode
3. Error correction: Add sequence numbers with gap detection and optional FEC (forward error correction)
4. Pipeline integration: tty-audio input → direct transcription (encode → decode → transcribe in one pipeline)
5. Opus codec option: For higher quality at same bandwidth, offer Opus as alternative to μ-law
6. Bandwidth estimation: Report actual bandwidth usage in robot mode events
7. Two-way relay: Support bidirectional audio for potential voice interaction scenarios

Use case: SSH into a remote server, speak into local mic, have remote franken_whisper transcribe in real-time, stream results back. All over a plain TTY connection.

Key files: src/tty_audio.rs (204 lines)
Codec chain: Input → ffmpeg → 8kHz mono μ-law → chunk → zlib → base64 → NDJSON

## Acceptance Criteria
- TTY audio codec encodes/decodes audio via mu-law + zlib + base64 NDJSON frames
- Round-trip preserves audio quality within acceptable SNR
- Pipeline integration allows TTY-sourced audio to feed into transcription
- Adaptive bitrate adjusts to available bandwidth
- All TTY audio tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: TTY audio codec encodes/decodes audio via mu-law + zlib + base64 NDJSON frames. Round-trip preserves audio quality within acceptable SNR. Pipeline integration allows TTY-sourced audio to feed into transcription. Adaptive bitrate adjusts to available bandwidth. All TTY audio tests pass.
close_reason: done

title: Integrate TTY audio with transcription pipeline
description:

Command: franken_whisper tty-audio transcribe --chunk-ms 200
Input: NDJSON audio frames on stdin
Output: NDJSON transcription events on stdout

Flow:
1. Read NDJSON audio frames from stdin
2. Decode and accumulate in buffer
3. When buffer reaches threshold (e.g., 10 seconds), send to backend
4. Stream partial transcript results back as NDJSON
5. Continue until EOF or Ctrl+C

Killer use case: SSH into remote server with GPU, send audio from local mic via TTY, get transcription back — all over a plain terminal connection.

All pipeline stages (normalize, backend, accelerate, persist) apply as normal. Only the input source changes (TTY NDJSON instead of file).

- Decoder reconstructs WAV from NDJSON frame stream
- Reconstructed WAV is accepted by ffmpeg normalization stage
- Unit test: encode then decode then transcribe produces valid result
- Integration test: cat frames.ndjson | cargo run -- tty-audio decode | cargo run -- transcribe works.

title: Add adaptive bitrate and error correction for TTY audio
description:
Enhance TTY audio for unreliable connections:

1. ADAPTIVE BITRATE: Monitor frame delivery latency. Increase compression if latency rises. Reduce compression when latency is low. Emit bitrate change events as NDJSON.

2. ERROR CORRECTION: Sequence numbers with gap detection (already present). Request retransmit or interpolate on decoder side. Optional FEC using fountain codes (RaptorQ) — same approach frankensqlite uses for WAL self-healing.

3. CONNECTION QUALITY METRICS: Track frame delivery rate, latency p50/p95, loss rate, jitter. Report as NDJSON events periodically. Drive adaptive bitrate decisions.

4. OPUS CODEC OPTION: For higher quality at same bandwidth. Opus at 16kbps significantly outperforms mu-law at 64kbps. Feature-gated behind --codec opus flag.

This is the alien-artifact approach to audio streaming: adaptive, self-healing, measured.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Codec adapts frame size based on measured throughput
- Lower bandwidth reduces frame size (fewer samples per frame)
- Higher bandwidth increases frame size (better compression ratio)
- Adaptation is smooth (no sudden jumps in frame size)
- Unit test: simulated slow pipe triggers smaller frames
- Unit test: simulated fast pipe allows larger frames.
acceptance_criteria: Codec adapts frame size based on measured throughput. Lower bandwidth reduces frame size (fewer samples per frame). Higher bandwidth increases frame size (better compression ratio). Adaptation is smooth (no sudden jumps in frame size). Unit test: simulated slow pipe triggers smaller frames. Unit test: simulated fast pipe allows larger frames.

title: Deep asupersync Integration: Cancel-Correct Orchestration Throughout
description:
EPIC: Deep asupersync Integration

Current state: franken_whisper uses asupersync minimally — just Runtime::new(2 workers, 1 blocking/4 parallelism), spawn, and block_on. This is a "shallow" integration that misses the entire point of asupersync.

Target state: Every pipeline stage flows through Cx capability contexts. Cancellation is a first-class protocol (request → drain → finalize). Resource cleanup is guaranteed via registered finalizers. Bounded cleanup budgets ensure deterministic shutdown times. Lab runtime enables injection testing at every cancellation point.

WHY this matters: The legacy whisper systems have NO cancellation story. A long transcription job that gets cancelled can leave temp files, orphan processes, partial DB writes, and corrupted state. asupersync's cancel-correctness guarantees eliminate this entire class of bugs.

asupersync's four structural guarantees we must leverage:
1. No Orphan Tasks — every spawned task owned by a region; region close waits for ALL children
2. Cancel-Correctness — cancellation as protocol, never silent data loss
3. Bounded Cleanup — cleanup budgets are sufficient conditions, not hopes
4. No Silent Drops — two-phase effects (reserve/commit) prevent data loss

Key integration points:
- Orchestrator pipeline: Each stage (ingest, normalize, backend, accelerate, persist) should be a Cx region
- Backend execution: Subprocess spawning should register finalizers for process cleanup
- Storage: All DB operations should receive &Cx for cancel-safety
- Temp files: Register cleanup finalizers so cancelled runs don't leak disk space
- Robot mode: Event streaming should respect cancellation signals
- TUI: Async event loop should integrate with asupersync runtime

## Acceptance Criteria
- All pipeline stages receive and use Cx capability context.
- Cancellation propagates from root to all child regions within 100ms.
- Finalizers registered for all temp files, subprocesses, and DB transactions.
- Bounded cleanup budgets enforce time limits per stage.
- Lab runtime tests verify cancel-correct behavior.
- Graceful Ctrl+C shutdown works end-to-end.

title: Register finalizers for temp files, subprocesses, and DB transactions
description:
asupersync's finalizer system ensures resources are cleaned up even when tasks are cancelled. Register finalizers for:

1. TEMP FILES (src/orchestrator.rs): Each run creates a temp directory under .franken_whisper/tmp. Register finalizer to delete on cancellation. Disarm on success.

2. SUBPROCESSES (src/process.rs, src/backend/*.rs): When spawning ffmpeg, whisper-cli, python. Register finalizer to send SIGTERM then SIGKILL after timeout. Prevents zombie processes.

3. DB TRANSACTIONS (src/storage.rs): On BEGIN, register finalizer for ROLLBACK. Disarm on COMMIT.

4. LOCK FILES (src/sync.rs): On lock acquire, register finalizer to release. Prevents stale locks.

UNIT TESTS REQUIRED (Definition of Done):
- test_temp_dir_finalizer: Create temp dir, register finalizer, trigger cancellation → dir deleted
- test_temp_dir_finalizer_disarm: Create temp dir, register finalizer, succeed → dir NOT deleted
- test_subprocess_finalizer: Spawn long-running process, register kill finalizer, cancel → process killed
- test_db_transaction_finalizer: BEGIN, register rollback finalizer, cancel → ROLLBACK executed, no partial data
- test_lock_file_finalizer: Acquire lock, register release finalizer, cancel → lock released
- test_nested_finalizers: Multiple finalizers fire in reverse registration order
- All tests use tracing to log finalizer registration and execution

LOGGING:
- "Registering finalizer for {resource_type}: {description}" at DEBUG

- "Finalizer disarmed for {resource_type}" at DEBUG

title: Implement bounded cleanup budgets per pipeline stage
description:
Bounded cleanup ensures that shutdown completes within a known time. Each pipeline stage should have a cleanup budget:

Stage budgets (proposed):
- ingest: 2s (file copy or stdin read should be fast)
- normalize: 5s (ffmpeg may need to flush buffers)
- backend: 10s (external process needs graceful shutdown)
- accelerate: 3s (GPU operations should be bounded)
- persist: 5s (DB transaction commit/rollback)

Total pipeline cleanup budget: 25s maximum

Implementation:
1. Set budget on each region: cx.with_budget(Budget::deadline(Duration::from_secs(10)))
2. If cleanup exceeds budget, escalate (log warning, force-kill)
3. Report actual cleanup times in run events for monitoring

This is especially important for the backend stage — if whisper-cli hangs during cancellation, we need to kill it after the budget expires rather than waiting forever.

The budgets should be configurable (environment variables or config file) for different deployment scenarios (a CI server might want tighter budgets than a desktop workstation).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each pipeline stage has a configurable cleanup budget (default: 5 seconds).
- Budget is enforced: if cleanup exceeds budget, remaining finalizers are skipped with warning.
- Budget inheritance: child regions inherit remaining parent budget.
- Unit test: cleanup budget exceeded triggers warning log.
- Unit test: normal cleanup within budget completes all finalizers.

title: Implement graceful Ctrl+C shutdown via asupersync cancellation protocol
description:

1. Set root cancellation token
2. Allow in-progress stages to drain gracefully
3. Run all registered finalizers (cleanup temp files, kill subprocesses, rollback DB)
4. Emit robot event: {"event": "run_cancelled", "run_id": "...", "stages_completed": [...], "cleanup_summary": {...}}
5. Exit with code 130 (SIGINT convention)

For TUI mode: Restore terminal state before exiting.
For robot mode: Cancelled event is valid NDJSON.

EPIC: Deep frankensqlite Integration

Current state: storage.rs uses frankensqlite at a basic level — Connection::open, execute, query with parameters, manual BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. This is barely better than raw rusqlite.

Target state: Leverage frankensqlite's two headline innovations:
1. MVCC Concurrent Writers — multiple transcription runs can persist simultaneously without blocking each other (page-level concurrency, SSI for write skew detection)
2. RaptorQ-Pervasive Architecture — self-healing WAL frames, quantitatively bounded data loss (not silent corruption)

- Schema versioning with migration support
- Index optimization for common query patterns (list by time, filter by backend, search transcript text)
- Aggregate views for statistics (runs per backend, average confidence, etc.)

frankensqlite is a LIBRARY, not a runtime — it expects callers to provide &Cx contexts from asupersync. This creates a natural integration point between the two deep dependencies.

title: Leverage MVCC for concurrent run persistence
description:
frankensqlite's headline innovation: MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) with page-level concurrent writers.

Current state: One run persists at a time (serial execution). With MVCC, multiple runs can write simultaneously without blocking each other.

Use case: When running two-lane execution (parallel backends), both results can be persisted concurrently. Or when the TUI is reading runs while a new transcription is being persisted.

Implementation:
1. Use frankensqlite's MVCC-aware connection mode
2. Each pipeline run gets its own transaction with snapshot isolation
3. Concurrent reads (TUI, robot list) never block concurrent writes
4. Write skew detection via SSI (Serializable Snapshot Isolation) prevents conflicts
5. Page-level First-Committer-Wins for same-page conflicts (rare for our schema since runs have unique IDs)

- All should persist successfully without blocking
- Verify no data corruption or missing records
- Check that reads during writes return consistent snapshots

title: P1 perf: built-in audio normalization vs ffmpeg batch dominance
description:
Target the realistic batch-ingest workload where franken_whisper can dominate original/scripted Whisper stacks by avoiding subprocess-heavy ffmpeg normalization for common formats.

Candidate levers:
- Reuse decode/resample/write buffers across files.
- Arena or bump allocation for per-run audio scratch.
- SIMD/auto-vectorized stereo mix, f32->i16 quantization, and linear resample loops.
- Branchless fast path for already-normalized 16k mono WAV.
- Cache-oblivious chunking for long audio to reduce peak RSS.

Required measurement:
- `normalize_bench` via rch, crate-scoped, dedicated CARGO_TARGET_DIR.
- Real files: MP3, FLAC, WAV passthrough, MP4/video fallback, 10min and 2h durations when fixtures exist.
- Head-to-head against the original stack normalization path (`ffmpeg`/`whisper.cpp` preprocessing) with original time, franken time, ratio, and RSS.
- Record every win/loss/noise result in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

Acceptance:
- At least one realistic common-audio workload has a measured >20% p95 or wall-time win vs the original preprocessing route, with no transcript/conformance drift.
- No gain or regressions are rejected, documented, and not shipped.
- Quality gates: fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test.

Fallback:
- If high-quality resampling is required or builtin decode fails, retain deterministic ffmpeg fallback and record fallback trigger/evidence.
notes: FINDING (BlackThrush): the core lever is ALREADY implemented. normalize_to_wav_with_timeout (src/audio.rs:128) uses the native symphonia decoder as the PRIMARY path (handles mp3/aac/flac/wav/ogg/alac/wavpack in-process, zero external deps); ffmpeg is fallback-only (exotic/video formats) or when FORCE_FFMPEG_NORMALIZE env is set. So franken_whisper already avoids OpenAI Whisper/whisper.cpp's per-file ffmpeg subprocess spawn + temp-wav I/O -> the 'native dominance over ffmpeg for batch' goal is met by the default. Remaining angle is only: (a) a head-to-head ratio measurement for the ledger (marginal at e2e — normalization is one-time, ~1-5%), and (b) resampler QUALITY (linear -> sinc; that's accuracy, not speed). No speed lever to ship here. Per-crate perf for franken_whisper is encoder-GEMM-bound (bd-4hc0) + decoder-logits-bandwidth-bound; normalization is not on the critical path.

description:

title: Add comprehensive TTY audio codec roundtrip and edge case tests
description:
The TTY audio module (src/tty_audio.rs, 204 lines) uses μ-law + zlib + base64. Needs thorough testing:

UNIT TESTS:
1. CODEC ROUNDTRIP:
   - Encode WAV to NDJSON frames → decode back → compare audio properties
   - Verify sample rate preserved (8kHz)
   - Verify channel count preserved (mono)
   - Log: Input size, frame count, total payload size, compression ratio

2. FRAME FORMAT:
   - Each frame has: seq (monotonic), codec (mulaw+zlib+b64), sample_rate_hz (8000), channels (1), payload_b64
   - Verify all fields present and valid
   - Verify base64 decoding produces valid zlib data
   - Verify zlib decompression produces valid μ-law data

3. CHUNK SIZE VARIATIONS:
   - Test chunk_ms: 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 5000

   - Verify all frames have correct payload size

   - Empty input → zero frames
   - Very short input (< 1 chunk) → single frame
   - Very long input (1 hour) → correct frame count, no memory issues
   - Frames out of order → sorted by seq before decode
   - Missing frames (gap in seq) → handled gracefully

5. COMPRESSION EFFICIENCY:
   - Measure compression ratio across different audio content
   - Silence should compress very well (>10x)
   - Speech should compress moderately (2-5x)
   - Random noise should compress poorly (<2x)
   - Log: Content type, raw size, compressed size, ratio

6. ERROR HANDLING:
   - Malformed JSON frame → skip with warning, continue
   - Invalid base64 → error with frame seq number
   - Corrupt zlib → error with frame seq number

title: P0 perf: ft-kernel-cpu sgemm matrixmultiply->gemm/faer (MEASURED 3.75x) — the e2e wall
description: MEASURED: franken_whisper's e2e is encoder-GEMM-bound, and the GEMM (ft_kernel_cpu::matmul_tensor_contiguous_f32) uses matrixmultiply 0.3 which is 3.75x SLOWER than gemm/faer for the encoder shape [1500,384]x[384,1536]: matrixmultiply 187 GFLOP/s vs gemm/faer 701 GFLOP/s (standalone, x86-64-v3, rayon). Swapping ft-kernel-cpu's matrixmultiply backend to the gemm crate (faer's backend) ~3.75x the sgemm -> ~2x the encoder -> ~1.2x e2e for franken_whisper (and benefits ALL frankentorch users). ft-kernel-cpu already uses unsafe matrixmultiply internally so gemm's unsafe API is fine there; franken_whisper's #![forbid(unsafe_code)] blocks calling gemm directly (faer's safe API is a heavy dep). This is the single biggest remaining e2e lever. Lives in the frankentorch crate (ft-kernel-cpu), out of franken_whisper-cc's scope — needs frankentorch owner or scope expansion.
notes: REFUTED (MEASURED, BlackThrush 2026-06-29). Standalone correctness-gated probe: the gemm crate (faer backend, Parallelism::Rayon(0)=64 threads, x86-64-v3) is TIED 1.01x on the EXACT named shape [1500,384]x[384,1536] (mm 254 vs gemm 252 GF/s) and 1.37x-3.13x SLOWER on production large-v3-turbo encoder shapes (large mlp proj: mm 634 vs gemm 203 GF/s = 3.1x slower). The bead's '187 GF/s matrixmultiply' measured RAW matrixmultiply, NOT ft_kernel_cpu::matmul_tensor_contiguous_f32's tuned rayon-blocked wrapper (kgs4.48/kgs4.61), which already beats the gemm crate. Swapping would REGRESS the encoder. faer-the-library wraps the same gemm microkernels so cannot exceed this ceiling. Full reproduction in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md (2026-06-29 BlackThrush). No encoder-GEMM lever exists here.
close_reason: Refuted by measurement: gemm/faer is tied-to-3.1x-slower than the production ft_kernel_cpu matmul on the real encoder shapes; would regress, not speed up. See docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-06-29 BlackThrush.

title: P0 perf: decoder ~2x SLOWER than whisper.cpp (the real vs-original gap) — profile + optimize
description: MEASURED head-to-head (bd-zk43, docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-06-25): franken tiny.en jfk decoder ~388ms vs whisper.cpp ~198ms = ~2x SLOWER, while franken's mel + encoder already WIN. So the real vs-whisper.cpp loss is the DECODER, and it is IN-SCOPE franken code (src/native_engine: gemv_f16 + the per-token decode loop), NOT the external GEMM (bd-4hc0 only extends an already-winning encoder). The session's gemv micro-benchmarks (FMA 0.79x, vertical-layout 1.03x, int8 0.24x) were franken-vs-franken and concluded 'mature' — but vs GGML there is ~2x headroom, so the bottleneck is likely NOT the raw dot8. Candidates to PROFILE per-token: (a) logits gemv [51864,384] vs GGML's f16 matmul (GGML may keep activations f16 / use a blocked f16 layout / different threading); (b) per-token overhead — allocations in forward_step, KV-cache growth handling, scratch buffers; (c) flash attention (whisper.cpp uses flash attn=1); (d) sampling/suppress-tokens cost. Method: instrument forward_step (mel/encode excluded), break down logits-gemv vs layers vs overhead, compare to whisper.cpp decode+sample (~7ms/token vs franken ~14ms/token). Record ratios in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md; REVERT ~0-gain.
notes: NEAR PARITY ACHIEVED (BlackThrush, 2026-06-25). 5 in-scope conformance-green decoder wins L9-L13: L9 mlp GEMV spawn threshold, L10 m=1 gemv (skip sgemm packing), L11 rayon persistent-pool gemv_f16, L12 rayon cross-attn (no-ts), L13 rayon cross-attn (record/ts path). Fresh back-to-back head-to-head: franken no-ts 486ms vs whisper.cpp ~452ms = 1.07x slower (was 1.37x at session start); franken realistic w/ DTW timestamps 504ms (was 614ms, -18%). The decoder gap was per-call thread::scope spawn (vs whisper.cpp's persistent pool) + sgemm-for-gemv at m=1 (vs GGML dedicated dot) -- both now fixed. Recorded in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md + PERF_LEDGER.md L9-L13. Remaining decoder is mature (gemv_f16 + softmax). Outright WIN now needs bd-4hc0 (encoder matrixmultiply->gemm, ~2x encoder; out-of-scope ft-kernel-cpu) -- franken's encoder already wins 204 vs 242ms, so the GEMM swap would push to a clear overall win. This bead's core (decoder ~2x gap) is RESOLVED to near-parity.

title: Profile diarization and noisy multi-speaker workloads vs original stack
description:
## Background
Real users care about meetings, interviews, noisy rooms, overlap, and speaker labels. The existing native-engine artifacts mostly prove ASR throughput on JFK and a long call; they do not measure full diarization/source-separation/VAD workloads against the original whisper-diarization or whisper.cpp TinyDiarize stack.

## Scope
Create a realistic multi-speaker corpus and profile end-to-end franken pipelines against original-stack comparators. Split results by requested feature: `--tiny-diarize`, full `--diarize`, `--vad`, noisy overlap, and long meeting. Only optimize a top-5 measured hotspot. Candidate one-lever families include VAD skip policy, chunk/range scheduling with seam-quality caps, source-separation budget gating, or calibrated backend routing for diarization.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparators: whisper.cpp TinyDiarize for built-in speaker-turn path; legacy whisper-diarization/pyannote stack for full diarization. Record dependency versions and HF-token-free vs token-required modes separately.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard composition B/F: tail-safe adaptive controller and policy-as-data controllers, only with deterministic fallback.
- Alien artifact contract: explicit state/action/loss/posterior/calibration for any routing or budget controller.
- Profiling skill: decompose tail into service, process I/O, queueing, and synchronization.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: latency wins that silently degrade speaker attribution. Safe mode: no promotion without diarization quality caps, segment invariants, text WER, speaker drift report, and deterministic fallback to current static policy.

## Validation
Artifacts: p50/p95/p99 wall, RSS, user CPU, speaker-drift metrics, WER, segment/timestamp conformance, dependency versions, and ratio rows against the original stack. Regressions and neutral results go to docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

## Success Criteria
A measured end-to-end win over at least one original diarization workload without quality regression, or a closed negative-evidence report that identifies the next deeper primitive.

title: native_engine/encoder.rs: whisper audio encoder forward
description:
Implement src/native_engine/encoder.rs: whisper audio encoder forward pass.

SPEC (exact whisper architecture):
- Input mel [n_mel, 3000] for a 30s window (A2).
- conv1: Conv1d(n_mel -> n_state, k=3, stride=1, pad=1) + GELU; conv2: Conv1d(n_state -> n_state, k=3, stride=2, pad=1) + GELU -> [1500, n_state] (time-major).
- + sinusoidal positional embedding (whisper sinusoid: length 1500, channels n_state, log timescale increment ln(10000)/(channels/2-1)) — compute, do NOT read from file (file has it? whisper ggml stores encoder.positional_embedding — USE THE FILE TENSOR for exactness).
- n_audio_layer blocks: x += attn(ln1(x)) [n_head, no mask]; x += mlp(ln2(x)) where mlp = Linear(n,4n)+GELU+Linear(4n,n).
- final ln_post. Output [1500, n_state] reused across all decoder tokens of that window; also precompute per-layer cross K/V projections for decoder (k = x @ Wk (no bias in whisper k!), v = x @ Wv + bv) — note whisper k-projection HAS NO BIAS (verify tensor list: no decoder...attn.key.bias in ggml; handle bias-absent matmuls).
- Weight name map from ggml: encoder.conv{1,2}.{weight,bias}, encoder.positional_embedding, encoder.blocks.N.{attn.query.weight/bias, attn.key.weight, attn.value.weight/bias, attn.out.weight/bias, attn_ln.weight/bias, mlp.0.weight/bias, mlp.2.weight/bias, mlp_ln.weight/bias}, encoder.ln_post.{weight,bias}. VERIFY exact names by dumping tiny.en tensor directory (A1 test prints sorted names -> commit as fixture tests/fixtures/native/tiny_en_tensor_names.txt).
TESTS: shape pipeline test with random small synthetic model (n_state 64, 2 layers — construct weights in-memory); numeric regression: encode jfk.wav window with tiny.en and assert encoder output mean/std/first-8-values against fixture captured ONCE and committed (tests/fixtures/native/jfk_tiny_encoder_stats.json) — guards against silent numeric drift; gated on model presence.

EncoderWeights::from_ggml loads+pre-transposes all linear weights ([out,in]->[in,out]), keeps conv weights flat [Cout,Cin,K], validates every tensor shape against hparams with tensor-named errors (handles ggml [len,1] conv biases). forward() runs conv1(k3 s1 p1)+gelu, conv2(k3 s2 p1)+gelu, transpose mel-major->time-major, adds file positional_embedding (no sinusoid recompute), per-layer residual bidirectional attention (q w+b, k w NO bias, v w+b, out w+b) + mlp(Linear n->4n + gelu + Linear 4n->n), final ln_post; checkpoint() between layers for cancellation. title: Alien-Artifact Engineering: Adaptive Controllers with Formal Guarantees
description:
EPIC: Alien-Artifact Engineering

The AGENTS.md mandates that any adaptive/runtime decision must include:
- Explicit state space
- Explicit actions
- Loss matrix
- Posterior/confidence terms
- Calibration metric
- Deterministic fallback trigger
- Evidence ledger artifact

No adaptive controller should ship without conservative fallback.

Application areas in franken_whisper:
1. Adaptive Backend Router: Choose backend based on input characteristics (duration, estimated noise, speaker count, available hardware). State space = {input features}. Actions = {backend choice}. Loss matrix = {quality × latency tradeoffs}. Fallback = whisper_cpp (most reliable).

2. Confidence Calibration: Raw confidence scores from different backends are on different scales. Need a calibrated posterior that means "P(word is correct) = confidence_score". Calibration metric = Brier score or ECE (Expected Calibration Error).

3. VAD Threshold Tuning: Voice activity detection threshold affects precision/recall tradeoff. Too aggressive = miss speech. Too conservative = process silence. Adaptive threshold based on audio characteristics.

4. Two-Lane Execution: Run two backends in parallel, compare results, pick the one with higher calibrated confidence. This is the "alien" approach — use redundancy to improve quality.

5. Streaming Quality Controller: When streaming, decide when to emit a "stable" partial transcript vs waiting for more context. State = {accumulated audio, current hypothesis, confidence}. Action = {emit, wait}. Loss = {latency vs accuracy}.

Each controller must produce an evidence ledger artifact documenting the decision process for auditability and debugging.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adaptive routing uses explicit state/action/loss/posterior/calibration framework
- Shadow mode emits routing evidence without affecting execution
- Two-lane parallel execution with quality selection works end-to-end
- Evidence ledger persists all routing decisions
- All alien-artifact contract tests pass.

Two-lane parallel execution with quality selection works end-to-end. Evidence ledger persists all routing decisions. All alien-artifact contract tests pass.

title: Design adaptive backend router with explicit state space and loss matrix
description:
ALIEN-ARTIFACT: Adaptive Backend Router

Per AGENTS.md, every adaptive controller must have explicit state space, actions, loss matrix, posterior, calibration metric, deterministic fallback trigger, evidence ledger artifact.

STATE SPACE: Audio duration, noise estimate (SNR), diarization requested, available backends, GPU capability, historical performance.
ACTIONS: Select backend, model size, processing mode.
LOSS MATRIX: quality × latency × resource tradeoffs.
POSTERIOR: P(quality | backend, input) from historical runs. Bayesian update.
CALIBRATION: Brier score.
DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK: If confidence < 0.3 or no history → static auto-selection.
EVIDENCE LEDGER: JSON artifact in events table, stage=adaptive_routing.

Note: README.md documents shadow-mode routing events. This formalizes that into full alien-artifact contract.

UNIT TESTS REQUIRED (Definition of Done):
- test_fallback_with_no_history: Zero historical runs → deterministic fallback used, fallback_triggered=true
- test_fallback_with_low_confidence: Posterior confidence < 0.3 → fallback used
- test_adaptive_with_history: 100+ runs → adaptive selection based on posterior
- test_loss_matrix_values: All cells in loss matrix are finite, non-negative
- test_evidence_ledger_complete: Every adaptive decision produces ledger with ALL required fields
- test_evidence_ledger_stored: Ledger written to events table as stage=adaptive_routing
- test_brier_score_computation: Known predictions + outcomes → correct Brier score
- test_shadow_mode_event: Auto-selection emits backend.routing.shadow event with full state/action/loss

LOGGING:
- "Adaptive routing: state={state_summary}, selected={action}, confidence={conf}" at INFO
- "Fallback triggered: {reason}" at WARN

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shadow routing event contains: state (backend availability, recent performance), action (selected backend), loss matrix (per-backend expected cost), posterior (confidence per backend), calibration metric (predicted vs actual accuracy)
- Event is emitted on every auto-mode run
- Unit test: shadow event contains all required fields
- Unit test: shadow event values are valid (probabilities sum to 1, loss values non-negative).

title: Implement confidence calibration with posterior and Brier score
description:
ALIEN-ARTIFACT: Confidence Calibration

Raw confidence scores from different backends are on different scales. A confidence of 0.8 from whisper_cpp does NOT mean the same as 0.8 from insanely_fast.

STATE SPACE: Raw confidence score (f64), backend that produced it (BackendKind), segment duration (seconds), audio quality estimate (SNR).

ACTIONS: Apply calibration function: calibrated = sigmoid(a * raw + b) per backend. Parameters a, b learned from historical data.

LOSS MATRIX: Overconfident (claim 0.9, actually wrong): high loss. Underconfident (claim 0.3, actually correct): medium loss. Well-calibrated: zero loss.

POSTERIOR: P(word_correct | confidence, backend) as logistic regression.

CALIBRATION METRIC: Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Bin predictions by confidence, compare mean confidence vs actual accuracy per bin. Target ECE < 0.05.

DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK: If < 100 historical data points: pass through raw confidence unchanged. If ECE > 0.15: disable calibration, fall back to raw scores.

Implementation: frankentorch tensor_sigmoid for calibration curve, tensor_backward for parameter fitting (offline). Store calibration parameters in frankensqlite _meta table. Update every 100 runs or on explicit recalibrate command.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Calibration metric tracks: predicted confidence vs actual quality over time
- Metric improves as more runs provide ground truth
- Calibration error (ECE) calculated and logged
- Unit test: perfect predictions produce zero calibration error
- Unit test: random predictions produce high calibration error
- Metric persisted in evidence ledger for trend analysis.

title: Implement two-lane execution: parallel backends with quality selection
description:
ALIEN-ARTIFACT: Two-Lane Execution

Run two backends in parallel, compare results, select the best. Use redundancy for quality.

STATE SPACE: Available backends (at least 2 required), audio input characteristics, time budget.

ACTIONS: Run backend A and B in parallel. Compare: confidence, segment count, transcript coherence. Select winner OR merge best segments from both.

LOSS MATRIX: Both succeed pick best (optimal, 2x cost). One fails other succeeds (failover benefit). Both fail (no worse than single). Time budget exceeded (cancel slower, use faster).

SELECTION CRITERIA (ranked): Higher calibrated mean confidence, more segments, better speaker separation, shorter processing time (tiebreaker).

DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK: If only one backend available: single-lane. If time budget < 2x expected time: single-lane.

Implementation: Use asupersync parallel regions (one per backend). Both write to temp dirs. Main region waits for both (or cancels slower after timeout). Compare using calibrated confidence scores. MVCC enables concurrent persistence.

This naturally exercises deep asupersync (parallel regions, cancellation, bounded cleanup) and deep frankensqlite (MVCC concurrent writes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Two backends execute in parallel on same input
- Quality comparison selects winner based on: confidence scores, segment alignment, timing precision
- Losing backend result discarded (or persisted as shadow)
- Parallel execution respects Cx cancellation
- Unit test: higher-quality result is selected
- Unit test: cancel during parallel execution cleans up both backends
- Performance: parallel overhead under 10% vs single backend.

title: Implement evidence ledger system for all adaptive decisions
description:
ALIEN-ARTIFACT: Evidence Ledger

Every adaptive decision produces an evidence ledger artifact for auditability.

Schema: controller, decision_id (UUID), timestamp (RFC3339), state (JSON), actions_considered (vec of {action, expected_loss, confidence}), action_selected, posterior, loss_estimate, calibration_metric, fallback_triggered, fallback_reason, outcome (post-hoc).

Storage: events table stage=evidence_ledger, also in JSONL export.
Query: robot evidence --run <id>, CLI evidence --last 10, TUI evidence pane.

UNIT TESTS REQUIRED (Definition of Done):
- test_ledger_schema_complete: Every ledger has ALL required fields populated
- test_ledger_uuid_unique: Each decision gets a unique ID
- test_ledger_timestamps_valid: All timestamps are valid RFC3339
- test_ledger_round_trip: Create → persist → load → compare (no data loss)
- test_ledger_query_by_run: Load all ledgers for a specific run_id
- test_ledger_query_recent: Load last N ledgers across all runs
- test_ledger_in_jsonl_export: Evidence ledgers included in JSONL export
- test_outcome_backfill: After execution, outcome field is populated

LOGGING:
- "Evidence ledger created: controller={ctrl}, decision={id}" at DEBUG
- "Evidence ledger outcome: {id} → {outcome_summary}" at DEBUG

## Acceptance Criteria
- Evidence ledger persists: every routing decision, shadow mode results, calibration updates, backend performance metrics
- Ledger stored in frankensqlite alongside run data
- Ledger queryable for trend analysis (which backend is improving/degrading)
- Unit test: routing decision persisted and retrievable
- Unit test: ledger grows monotonically (append-only)
- Export: ledger included in JSONL sync exports.

title: franken-decision to_evidence_ledger() panics on the degenerate native-only fallback audit (worked around in backend/mod.rs)
description:
UPSTREAM (franken-decision crate, v0.3.4/0.3.5).

On a native-only install (no external whisper.cpp / insanely-fast / whisper-diarization BRIDGE backend present) the adaptive router computes observed_state == 2 ("no bridge backends"). franken-decision's decision_evaluate then engages the deterministic fallback and returns an internally-inconsistent DecisionAuditEntry. Converting that entry via its own DecisionAuditEntry::to_evidence_ledger() (which calls EvidenceLedgerBuilder::build().expect("audit entry should produce valid evidence ledger")) PANICS:

  Validation([PosteriorNotNormalized { sum: -0.0 },
              CalibrationOutOfRange { value: 0.5 },
              ChosenExpectedLossMismatch { action: "try_whisper_cpp", chosen: -0.0, mapped: -0.0 }])

i.e. franken-decision produces an audit that its own builder rejects, and the conversion PANICS (via .expect) instead of returning an error — killing every transcription on the common native-only path.

Repro: `franken_whisper youtube <url>` (or `transcribe` with backend=auto) on a machine whose only usable backend is the native engine. The in-process decoder falls back to ffmpeg, routing evaluates, and the panic aborts the run.

ROOT CAUSE (in franken-decision): the fallback branch of decision_evaluate emits an audit with an empty/unnormalized posterior_snapshot and a chosen expected_loss that does not match expected_loss_by_action[chosen]; and to_evidence_ledger() uses .expect() rather than returning Result.

RECOMMENDED UPSTREAM FIX: (a) decision_evaluate must not emit an unbuildable audit for the fallback branch — populate/normalize posterior_snapshot and keep chosen expected_loss == expected_loss_by_action[chosen]; and/or (b) DecisionAuditEntry::to_evidence_ledger() should return Result<EvidenceLedger, _> instead of panicking.

WORKAROUND ALREADY LANDED in franken_whisper (src/backend/mod.rs, the routing decision function): the evidence ledger is a diagnostic, so guard its construction — skip the conversion when the audit posterior is empty/unnormalized (the observed degeneracy), with catch_unwind as a safety net, degrading to no evidence entry and recording an 'evidence_ledger_conversion_failed' router event. Mirrors the existing "diagnostics never kill transcription" guards (failed posterior update, contract-validation fallback).

VERIFIED: patched native-only `transcribe` returns real segments with zero panics on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

title: EPIC: Real native whisper inference engine on frankentorch (replaces mock pilots)
description:
GOAL: Replace the mock native-engine pilots (WhisperCppPilot/InsanelyFastPilot/DiarizationPilot in src/backend/mod.rs:3241-3587, which emit canned phrases like "The quick brown fox...") with a REAL pure-Rust Whisper inference engine so the native rollout machinery (Shadow->Validated->Fallback->Primary->Sole) governs a real engine, as the README promises.

ARCHITECTURE DECISION (settled with Jeffrey 2026-06-04):
- Build on frankentorch crates (path deps ../frankentorch/crates/*): ft-kernel-cpu provides rayon-parallel sgemm/sgemm_block (matrixmultiply-backed), softmax_dim_tensor_contiguous_f32, gelu; ft-core provides DenseTensor with F16/F32 storage (half crate); ft-serialize provides load_safetensors (f16->f32). Assessed 2026-06-04: 1821/1822 tests pass, real kernels, no heavy deps.
- franken_whisper implements the whisper-specific layer: ggml .bin parser, log-mel frontend, BPE tokenizer, encoder/decoder assembly with KV cache, decode loop. Use a THIN internal facade that calls ft-kernel-cpu kernels directly (avoids ft-api tape overhead per decoder token; keeps KV cache management local).
- frankenjax (fj-interpreters/fj-lax) = optional differential-verification oracle for attention/softmax numerics in the conformance harness (feature-gated; it is scalar-loop slow but oracle-verified against real JAX).
- New module dir src/native_engine/ (genuinely new functionality, sanctioned exception to no-new-files rule).
- forbid(unsafe_code) stays. No FFI. New non-optional path deps: ft-kernel-cpu, ft-core (and ft-serialize for Epic B). Keep gpu-* features unchanged (accelerate stage).

MODEL FORMAT GROUND TRUTH (verified against ~/models/whisper/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin and ggml-tiny.en.bin 2026-06-04):
- magic 0x67676d6c ("lmgg" LE); 11 x i32 hparams: n_vocab, n_audio_ctx, n_audio_state, n_audio_head, n_audio_layer, n_text_ctx, n_text_state, n_text_head, n_text_layer, n_mels, ftype. (large-v3-turbo: 51866/1500/1280/20/32/448/1280/20/4/128/1)
- mel filterbank embedded: i32 n_mel, i32 n_fft_bins, then n_mel*n_fft_bins f32 (128x201 for v3).
- vocab: i32 n_vocab_in_file (50257 for both), then per token: i32 len + raw bytes. Multilingual specials beyond file vocab are synthesized by id (replicate whisper.cpp logic).
- tensor directory until EOF: i32 n_dims, i32 name_len, i32 ftype, n_dims x i32 dims, name bytes, then data aligned; ftype 0=f32 1=f16 (quantized variants exist; f32/f16 required, quantized = follow-up bead).

PERFORMANCE EXPECTATION: tiny/base near-real-time on 8-16 cores; large-v3-turbo functional but slow on CPU (~1-2x audio duration). That is FINE: the rollout governance keeps the bridge primary until the native engine earns promotion via conformance + benchmarks. Honesty first, speed second.

SUCCESS CRITERIA: franken_whisper transcribe --backend whisper-cpp with FRANKEN_WHISPER_NATIVE_EXECUTION=1 FRANKEN_WHISPER_NATIVE_ROLLOUT_STAGE=sole produces a real transcript of tests fixture jfk.wav with tiny.en whose WER vs whisper-cli output is <= 0.10; zero canned phrases anywhere in src/; cargo fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test all green.

title: native_engine/nn.rs: inference kernels facade over ft-kernel-cpu + KV-cache attention
description:
Implement src/native_engine/nn.rs: inference micro-ops facade over frankentorch kernels + attention with KV cache.

SPEC:
- Thin row-major matrix type Mat { rows, cols, data: Vec<f32> } (weights pre-transposed at load time so all matmuls are [m,k]x[k,n] contiguous).
- matmul: delegate to ft_kernel_cpu::sgemm/sgemm_block (rayon-parallel, matrixmultiply-backed). Add franken_whisper-side wrapper choosing block strategy by shape (decoder steps are [1,k]x[k,n] GEMV-shaped: benchmark sgemm vs hand-rolled parallel dot loops; pick faster, keep both behind one fn).
- layer_norm(x, w, b, eps=1e-5) (rows independent, rayon over rows); gelu (exact tanh approximation matching whisper.cpp: 0.5x(1+tanh(sqrt(2/pi)(x+0.044715x^3)))); softmax rows (delegate ft kernel or local stable impl — must be the bit-stable one already used by accelerate.rs? unify later, keep local for now).
- conv1d(x[T,Cin], w[Cout,Cin,K], b, stride, pad=1) via im2col + sgemm.
- MultiHeadAttention fn with: pre-projected qkv weights, n_head, optional causal mask, KV cache append (self-attn) and static cross K/V (precomputed once per window from encoder output). Scale = (d_head)^-0.25 applied to BOTH q and k (whisper convention) — VERIFY vs whisper.cpp (it scales q by d^-0.25 and k by d^-0.25 in some impls, or qk by d^-0.5; match numerically).
- All loops must call CancellationToken-style checkpoint via a passed-in &dyn Fn() -> FwResult<()> every block (project cancellation contract).
TESTS: matmul vs naive triple loop (rand, rel<1e-5); layernorm/gelu/softmax vs scalar reference; attention vs naive full-recompute reference incl. cache-consistency property (incremental decode == full recompute, 1e-4); OPTIONAL feature "fj-oracle": cross-check softmax+matmul against frankenjax eval_primitive (fj-lax Dot) as differential oracle. Criterion bench file benches/native_engine_bench.rs covering sgemm shapes for tiny/large decoder step.

title: native_engine/decoder.rs: whisper text decoder forward + KV cache
description:
Implement src/native_engine/decoder.rs: whisper text decoder forward with KV cache.

SPEC:
- Token embedding (decoder.token_embedding.weight [n_vocab, n_state]) + learned positional embedding (decoder.positional_embedding [n_text_ctx, n_state]) at position = cache_len.
- n_text_layer blocks: x += self_attn(ln1(x), causal, kv_cache append); x += cross_attn(ln_cross(x), encoder K/V precomputed); x += mlp(ln2(x)). NOTE whisper block layout: attn_ln -> attn -> cross_attn_ln -> cross_attn -> mlp_ln -> mlp (verify name map: decoder.blocks.N.{attn_ln, attn.*, cross_attn_ln, cross_attn.*, mlp_ln, mlp.*}).
- final decoder.ln; logits = x @ token_embedding^T (weight tying; only need LAST row's logits during decode — compute logits for final position only: [1,n_state] x [n_state, n_vocab] sgemm).
- KV cache: per layer Vec<f32> capacity n_text_ctx*n_state, tracked len; supports reset per window and truncation for prompt reuse.
- Cross K/V: computed once per window from encoder output (A5), passed in.
- Cross-attention weights of selected heads must be RECORDABLE (flag) into [n_head, tokens, 1500] buffer for A10 word timestamps via DTW.
TESTS: synthetic-weights shape/causality tests (token t logits independent of future tokens — property test); cache==full-recompute equivalence; gated numeric: greedy-decode first 5 tokens of jfk.wav with tiny.en and assert exact token ids equal fixture captured from whisper-cli -oj (tests/fixtures/native/jfk_tiny_tokens.json from A3).

title: Measure live/speculative streaming TTFT vs original streaming baselines
description:
## Background
`franken_whisper` claims real-time NDJSON and speculative dual-model streaming, but the current perf artifacts focus on batch transcription. For real users and agents, time-to-first-token/partial, correction latency, and p95 event latency matter as much as total wall time.

## Scope
Build a live/streaming benchmark that compares franken robot/speculative output against original streaming-capable baselines where available (`whisper.cpp` partial output or other original Whisper streaming harness). Measure TTFT, partial cadence, p95 event latency, correction/retraction rate, end-to-end wall, and quality drift. Optimize only after profiling a top-5 hotspot.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparator: `whisper.cpp` streaming/partial mode when available; otherwise explicitly label the baseline as OpenAI/whisper.cpp batch fallback and do not claim streaming superiority. Franken paths: robot NDJSON, speculative fast+quality, and TTY transcript-control path if exercised.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard composition B: tail-safe adaptive controller for speculation windows.
- Graveyard sections 12.1, 12.13, 12.16: conformal/calibration/change-point guards for correction thresholds.
- Alien artifact contract: state space, actions, loss, posterior/confidence, calibration, deterministic fallback, evidence ledger.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: better TTFT with unacceptable correction churn or WER. Safe mode: fixed deterministic window and current correction tolerance. Fallback trigger: Brier/coverage breach, correction-rate SLO breach, WER regression, or p95 latency regression.

## Validation
Artifacts: TTFT/TPOT-like metrics, p50/p95/p99 event latency, correction stats, WER drift, calibration ledger snapshot, original-vs-franken ratio row, conformance/golden output, and negative-evidence row for abandoned adaptive policies.

## Success Criteria

title: Pipeline Enhancement: Advanced Multi-Stage ASR Processing
description:
EPIC: Pipeline Enhancement

The current pipeline has 5 stages: ingest → normalize → backend → accelerate → persist. This is a good start but misses several powerful capabilities from the legacy systems.

New stages to add (inspired by whisper-diarization's multi-stage approach):
1. VAD Pre-filtering: Voice Activity Detection to identify speech segments before sending to ASR. Dramatically reduces processing time for audio with lots of silence/noise. Inspired by whisper.cpp's Silero-VAD integration.
2. Source Separation: Isolate vocals from background noise/music (Demucs-inspired). Improves speaker embedding accuracy and ASR quality on noisy audio.
3. Forced Alignment: CTC-based timestamp correction after initial ASR. Whisper's timestamps can drift at segment boundaries; forced alignment uses emission probabilities to find true boundaries. Critical for accurate word-level speaker mapping.
4. Speaker Diarization: TitaNet-inspired speaker embedding + clustering. Identify who said what. Currently delegated entirely to backends; bringing this in-house gives more control.
5. Punctuation Restoration: Multilingual punctuation model (12+ languages). The diarization pipeline strips punctuation during alignment; restoration makes transcripts readable.

Pipeline should also support:
- Skip/include stages based on request (e.g., skip diarization if not needed)
- Stage-level caching (don't re-normalize if already WAV)
- Parallel stage execution where possible (e.g., VAD + source separation)
- Progress reporting per stage (for robot mode and TUI)

Each new stage must follow the existing EventLog pattern — emit stage start/complete events with payloads for observability.

Key architectural decision: New stages should be composable and optional, not monolithic. The pipeline configuration should be declarative.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pipeline includes all stages: ingest, normalize, VAD, source separation, backend, alignment, diarization, punctuation, accelerate, persist
- Stages are composable and independently testable
- Each stage emits robot events
- Pipeline handles errors at any stage with proper cleanup
- All pipeline tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline includes all stages: ingest, normalize, VAD, source separation, backend, alignment, diarization, punctuation, accelerate, persist. Stages are composable and independently testable. Each stage emits robot events. Pipeline handles errors at any stage with proper cleanup. All pipeline tests pass.

title: Add forced alignment stage (CTC-based timestamp correction)
description:
Forced alignment corrects ASR timestamp drift using CTC emission probabilities. Whisper's timestamps can drift 0.5-2 seconds at segment boundaries; forced alignment finds the true word boundaries.

Inspiration: whisper-diarization uses ctc-forced-aligner.

Why this matters: Word-level speaker attribution requires precise word boundaries. Without forced alignment, speaker boundaries will be wrong.

Implementation:
1. BRIDGE MODE: Call ctc-forced-aligner via Python. Input: audio WAV + transcript text. Output: word-level timestamps with alignment scores.
2. POST-BACKEND STAGE: Runs AFTER backend produces initial transcript. Takes transcript text + original audio → produces aligned word timestamps. These replace the backend's less-accurate timestamps.

Pipeline position: backend → [forced_alignment] → accelerate → persist
Events: alignment.start, alignment.ok with aligned_words_count, alignment_score payload

- Works with output from any backend

- Stage emits robot event with alignment statistics.

title: Speculative Cancel-Correct Streaming: The Core Differentiator
description:
EPIC: Speculative Cancel-Correct Streaming (SCS)

WHY THIS EXISTS:
The entire franken_whisper architecture -- asupersync Cx, TwoLaneExecutor, CancellationToken, PipelineCx, the alien-artifact controller with evidence ledger, the TTY streaming protocol, robot mode event schema -- was designed around one thesis: partial transcription results that formally self-correct as better evidence arrives. Without this capability, the architecture is a beautifully tested skeleton wrapping a worse whisper.cpp. With it, franken_whisper becomes the only local ASR system with formally-verified incremental self-correction.

WHAT IT DOES:
1. Audio arrives (file, mic, TTY)
2. A FAST model (whisper-tiny equivalent) produces instant (~100ms) partial transcription results
3. Simultaneously, a QUALITY model (whisper-large equivalent) processes the same audio window
4. When the quality model finishes, it compares with the fast model output
5. If they differ beyond a configurable tolerance, a formal retract event is emitted for the fast result, followed by a correct event with the quality result
6. The evidence ledger tracks correction rates per-window
7. The alien-artifact controller adaptively tunes the speculation window size:
   - Bigger windows = fewer corrections but higher latency
   - Smaller windows = more corrections but snappier feel
8. Everything flows through cancel-correct semantics via asupersync Cx

WHAT IT MAKES LOAD-BEARING:
- PipelineCx / CancellationToken (orchestrator.rs) -- cancellation checkpoints between fast/quality runs
- TwoLaneExecutor (backend/mod.rs) -- parallel fast+quality execution
- AdaptiveBackendRouter / RoutingEvidenceLedger (backend/mod.rs) -- learns from correction history

title: Extend TTY protocol with transcript correction control frames
description:
PHASE 4 SURFACE INTEGRATION -- Adds correction-aware control frames to the TTY streaming protocol.

FILE: src/tty_audio.rs (extend existing)

WHY:
The TTY protocol currently handles audio frames and control frames (handshake, ack, retransmit, backpressure). For speculative streaming over TTY, the protocol needs to carry transcript events alongside audio. A remote consumer receiving audio+transcript over a TTY connection must be able to receive retract/correct events inline with the NDJSON stream.

CURRENT TTY PROTOCOL:
- TtyAudioFrame: audio data with seq, codec, integrity hashes
- TtyControlFrame: Handshake, HandshakeAck, RetransmitRequest/Response, Ack, Backpressure
- NDJSON line-oriented transport

WHAT TO ADD:

1. New TtyControlFrame variants:
   #[serde(rename = "transcript_partial")]
   TranscriptPartial {
       seq: u64,
       window_id: u64,
       segments: Vec<TranscriptSegmentCompact>,  // Compact form for wire
       model_id: String,
       speculative: bool,         // true = fast model, may be corrected
   },
   #[serde(rename = "transcript_retract")]
   TranscriptRetract {
       retracted_seq: u64,
       window_id: u64,
       reason: String,
   },
   #[serde(rename = "transcript_correct")]
   TranscriptCorrect {
       correction_id: u64,
       replaces_seq: u64,
       window_id: u64,
       segments: Vec<TranscriptSegmentCompact>,
       model_id: String,
       drift_wer: f64,
   },

2. TranscriptSegmentCompact (wire-efficient):
   pub struct TranscriptSegmentCompact {
       pub s: f64,       // start_sec (short field name for wire efficiency)
       pub e: f64,       // end_sec
       pub t: String,    // text
       pub sp: Option<String>,  // speaker
       pub c: Option<f64>,      // confidence
   }

3. Protocol version bump:
   - Bump SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION from 1 to 2
   - Version 2 adds transcript control frames
   - Version 1 clients that receive transcript frames should ignore them (forward compatibility)
   - Version negotiation during handshake determines whether transcript frames are sent

4. Emission helpers:
   pub fn emit_tty_transcript_partial(writer: &mut impl Write, seq: u64, window_id: u64, segments: &[TranscriptionSegment], model_id: &str, speculative: bool) -> FwResult<()>
   pub fn emit_tty_transcript_retract(writer: &mut impl Write, retracted_seq: u64, window_id: u64, reason: &str) -> FwResult<()>
   pub fn emit_tty_transcript_correct(writer: &mut impl Write, correction: &CorrectionEvent) -> FwResult<()>

DESIGN CHOICE -- WHY INLINE WITH AUDIO NDJSON:
- The TTY protocol is already NDJSON, so transcript events fit naturally
- Keeping audio and transcript in the same stream preserves temporal ordering
- A separate channel would require synchronization and add complexity
- The "type" field already distinguishes audio frames from control frames

WIRE FORMAT EXAMPLE:
{"type":"tty_audio","protocol_version":2,"seq":100,"codec":"mulaw+zlib+b64",...}
{"type":"transcript_partial","seq":1,"window_id":1,"segments":[{"s":0.0,"e":1.5,"t":"hello world","c":0.92}],"model_id":"whisper-tiny","speculative":true}
{"type":"tty_audio","protocol_version":2,"seq":101,...}
{"type":"transcript_retract","retracted_seq":1,"window_id":1,"reason":"quality model correction"}
{"type":"transcript_correct","correction_id":1,"replaces_seq":1,"window_id":1,"segments":[{"s":0.0,"e":1.5,"t":"hello world!","c":0.98}],"model_id":"whisper-large","drift_wer":0.05}

WHY:
The robot mode event schema (robot.rs) currently has these event types:

It does NOT have retract or correct events. Without these, downstream consumers (agents, TUI, logs) cannot distinguish between "new partial result" and "correction of a previous result." The cancel-correct contract requires formal, machine-parseable retraction semantics.

WHAT TO ADD:

1. New event type: "transcript.retract"

   - quality_model_id: String    // Which model triggered the retraction

2. New event type: "transcript.correct"

   - quality_model_id: String
   - drift: { wer_approx, confidence_delta, segment_count_delta, text_edit_distance }
   - latency_ms: u64             // Quality model latency
   - ts: String (RFC3339)

3. New event type: "transcript.speculation_stats"
   Periodic summary of speculation pipeline performance.
   Required fields:
   - event: "transcript.speculation_stats"
   - schema_version: ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION
   - run_id: String
   - windows_processed: u64
   - corrections_emitted: u64
   - correction_rate: f64         // corrections / windows
   - mean_fast_latency_ms: f64
   - mean_quality_latency_ms: f64
   - current_window_size_ms: u64  // Current adaptive window size
   - mean_drift_wer: f64
   - ts: String (RFC3339)

IMPLEMENTATION:

A. Add constants:
   const TRANSCRIPT_RETRACT_REQUIRED_FIELDS: &[&str] = &["event", "schema_version", "run_id", "retracted_seq", "window_id", "reason", "ts"];
   const TRANSCRIPT_CORRECT_REQUIRED_FIELDS: &[&str] = &["event", "schema_version", "run_id", "correction_id", "replaces_seq", "window_id", "segments", "drift", "ts"];
   const SPECULATION_STATS_REQUIRED_FIELDS: &[&str] = &["event", "schema_version", "run_id", "windows_processed", "corrections_emitted", "correction_rate", "ts"];

   pub fn emit_transcript_correct(run_id: &str, correction: &CorrectionEvent) -> FwResult<()>
   pub fn emit_speculation_stats(run_id: &str, stats: &SpeculationStats) -> FwResult<()>

   All new events must pass the same JSON-schema validation pattern as existing events.
   The retract+correct pair must be emitted atomically (retract line immediately before correct line, no interleaving).

DESIGN CHOICE -- WHY SEPARATE RETRACT AND CORRECT EVENTS:
- A consumer that only cares about final text can ignore retract events and just use the latest correct
- A consumer that wants to show corrections in real-time (TUI) needs both
- A consumer doing latency analysis needs the retract timestamp separately from the correct timestamp
- This matches the asupersync cancel-correct pattern where cancel and correct are distinct operations

- retract events MUST reference a previously-emitted transcript.partial seq
