title: Make TwoLaneExecutor concurrent with thread-based parallel execution
description:
PHASE 1 FOUNDATION -- Converts TwoLaneExecutor from sequential to truly parallel execution.

FILE: src/backend/mod.rs (modify existing TwoLaneExecutor)

WHY:
The existing TwoLaneExecutor (backend/mod.rs:3260-3354) runs primary_fn and secondary_fn SEQUENTIALLY. For speculative streaming, the fast model and quality model MUST run in parallel -- the entire value proposition is that the fast model result is available immediately while the quality model is still running. Sequential execution would make the total latency = fast + quality, defeating the purpose.

CURRENT STATE:
```rust
pub struct TwoLaneExecutor { selector: QualitySelector }
impl TwoLaneExecutor {
    pub fn execute<F1, F2>(&self, primary_fn: F1, secondary_fn: F2) -> TwoLaneResult
    where F1: FnOnce() -> Vec<TranscriptSegment>,
          F2: FnOnce() -> Vec<TranscriptSegment>
    // Currently runs primary_fn(), then secondary_fn() sequentially
}
```

TARGET STATE:
```rust
pub struct ConcurrentTwoLaneExecutor { selector: QualitySelector }
impl ConcurrentTwoLaneExecutor {
    pub fn execute<F1, F2>(&self, primary_fn: F1, secondary_fn: F2) -> TwoLaneResult
    where F1: FnOnce() -> Vec<TranscriptSegment> + Send + 'static,
          F2: FnOnce() -> Vec<TranscriptSegment> + Send + 'static
    // Spawns both on std::thread, joins both, then selects
}

impl ConcurrentTwoLaneExecutor {
    /// Execute with early emission: calls on_primary as soon as primary finishes,
    /// then waits for secondary and calls on_compare with both results.
    pub fn execute_with_early_emit<F1, F2, P, C>(
        &self,
        primary_fn: F1,
        secondary_fn: F2,
        on_primary: P,
        on_compare: C,
    ) -> TwoLaneResult
    where
        F1: FnOnce() -> Vec<TranscriptSegment> + Send + 'static,
        F2: FnOnce() -> Vec<TranscriptSegment> + Send + 'static,
        P: FnOnce(&[TranscriptSegment], u64),  // Called when primary finishes (segments, latency_ms)
        C: FnOnce(&[TranscriptSegment], &[TranscriptSegment], u64, u64) -> TwoLaneResult,
    {
        // 1. Spawn primary_fn on thread A
        // 2. Spawn secondary_fn on thread B
        // 3. Wait for thread A -> call on_primary(result_a, latency_a)
        // 4. Wait for thread B
        // 5. Call on_compare(result_a, result_b, latency_a, latency_b)
    }
}
```

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- Use std::thread::spawn (not async/tokio) to stay within the project's sync architecture
- Measure latency with std::time::Instant for each lane
- The existing sequential TwoLaneExecutor should be PRESERVED (not deleted) for backward compatibility and for cases where parallelism isn't needed
- ConcurrentTwoLaneExecutor is a NEW struct alongside the existing one
- The execute_with_early_emit method is the KEY innovation: it lets the pipeline emit fast-model results immediately while still waiting for the quality model

title: Implement WindowManager for audio chunking with configurable overlap
description:
PHASE 2 CORE MACHINERY -- Manages the audio stream as a sequence of overlapping windows.

FILE: src/speculation.rs (extend, same module as scs.1 types)

WHY:
Streaming ASR requires chopping continuous audio into fixed-size windows. But naive chopping cuts words at window boundaries, producing garbage at the edges. The WindowManager solves this by:
1. Maintaining configurable overlap between adjacent windows (typically 200-500ms)
2. Tracking window state (pending, fast-complete, quality-complete, corrected)
3. Providing the audio bytes for each window to both fast and quality models
4. Deduplicating overlapping segments when merging results

THE OVERLAP PROBLEM:
If window 1 covers 0-3000ms and window 2 covers 2500-5500ms (500ms overlap), both windows will transcribe the audio around 2500-3000ms. Without deduplication, you'd get duplicate text. The WindowManager must:
- Track which segments came from which window
- When merging, prefer the segment whose window center is closest to the segment's timestamp
- Use CorrectionDrift to detect when overlap segments differ significantly

TYPES AND INTERFACE:

pub struct WindowManager {
    window_size_ms: u64,          // Current window size (adaptive, changes over time)
    overlap_ms: u64,              // Overlap between adjacent windows
    min_window_ms: u64,           // Floor for adaptive sizing (e.g., 1000ms)
    max_window_ms: u64,           // Ceiling for adaptive sizing (e.g., 30000ms)
    next_window_id: u64,          // Monotonically increasing
    run_id: String,
    windows: Vec<WindowState>,    // All windows in this run
}

pub struct WindowState {
    pub window: SpeculationWindow,
    pub fast_result: Option<PartialTranscript>,
    pub quality_result: Option<Vec<TranscriptionSegment>>,
    pub status: WindowStatus,
}

pub enum WindowStatus {
    Pending,            // Audio sliced, not yet sent to models
    FastInProgress,     // Fast model is running
    FastComplete,       // Fast model done, quality model still running
    QualityComplete,    // Both models done, correction decision pending
    Resolved,           // Correction decision made (confirmed or corrected)
}

impl WindowManager {
    pub fn new(run_id: &str, window_size_ms: u64, overlap_ms: u64) -> Self
    pub fn next_window(&mut self, audio_position_ms: u64, audio_hash: &str) -> SpeculationWindow
    pub fn record_fast_result(&mut self, window_id: u64, partial: PartialTranscript)
    pub fn record_quality_result(&mut self, window_id: u64, segments: Vec<TranscriptionSegment>)
    pub fn resolve_window(&mut self, window_id: u64, status: WindowStatus)
    pub fn set_window_size(&mut self, new_size_ms: u64)  // Called by adaptive controller
    pub fn current_window_size(&self) -> u64
    pub fn windows_resolved(&self) -> usize
    pub fn windows_pending(&self) -> usize
    pub fn merge_segments(&self) -> Vec<TranscriptionSegment>  // Deduplicated, ordered
    pub fn overlap_segments(&self, window_id: u64) -> Vec<&TranscriptionSegment>
}

SEGMENT DEDUPLICATION ALGORITHM:
When two windows overlap and both produce segments in the overlap zone:
1. For each segment in the overlap, compute which window's center is closer
2. Keep the segment from the closer window
3. If within 50ms of the midpoint, keep the one with higher confidence
4. Log the deduplication decision in the evidence ledger

ADAPTIVE WINDOW SIZE:
The WindowManager accepts window size changes from the SpeculationWindowController (scs.7). It applies the new size to the NEXT window, never retroactively. Window size is clamped to [min_window_ms, max_window_ms].

title: Implement CorrectionTracker state machine for retraction/correction lifecycle
description:
PHASE 2 CORE MACHINERY -- The heart of cancel-correct: tracks every partial, decides corrections, emits retract/correct events.

FILE: src/speculation.rs (extend)

WHY:
When the quality model finishes, something must decide: "Is this different enough from the fast model's output to warrant a formal correction?" The CorrectionTracker owns this decision. It:
1. Receives fast model results as they arrive
2. Receives quality model results when they finish
3. Computes CorrectionDrift between them
4. Applies a configurable tolerance threshold
5. Emits either a Confirm (fast was good enough) or a Retract+Correct pair
6. Maintains running statistics for the adaptive controller

THIS IS THE CANCEL-CORRECT CONTRACT:
- Every PartialTranscript that enters the tracker MUST eventually be either Confirmed or Retracted
- No partial can be silently dropped
- Retraction is formal and observable (event emitted)
- The tracker guarantees that for any given window_id, exactly one authoritative result exists

TYPES AND INTERFACE:

pub struct CorrectionTracker {
    tolerance: CorrectionTolerance,
    partials: HashMap<u64, PartialTranscript>,  // Keyed by seq
    corrections: Vec<CorrectionEvent>,
    stats: CorrectionStats,
}

pub struct CorrectionTolerance {
    pub max_wer: f64,              // Maximum WER before triggering correction (e.g., 0.1 = 10%)
    pub max_confidence_delta: f64, // Maximum confidence difference (e.g., 0.15)
    pub max_edit_distance: usize,  // Maximum Levenshtein distance
    pub always_correct: bool,      // If true, always use quality model (useful for evaluation)
}

pub struct CorrectionStats {
    pub windows_processed: u64,
    pub corrections_emitted: u64,
    pub confirmations_emitted: u64,
    pub total_fast_latency_ms: u64,
    pub total_quality_latency_ms: u64,
    pub cumulative_wer: f64,       // Sum of all WER values (for computing mean)
    pub max_observed_wer: f64,
}

pub enum CorrectionDecision {
    Confirm {
        seq: u64,
        drift: CorrectionDrift,
    },
    Correct {
        correction: CorrectionEvent,
    },
}

impl CorrectionTracker {
    pub fn new(tolerance: CorrectionTolerance) -> Self
    
    /// Register a fast model result. Returns the seq for tracking.
    pub fn register_partial(&mut self, partial: PartialTranscript) -> u64
    
    /// Submit quality model result for a window. Returns the correction decision.
    /// This is the core method: it computes drift, applies tolerance, and decides.
    pub fn submit_quality_result(
        &mut self,
        window_id: u64,
        quality_model_id: &str,
        quality_segments: Vec<TranscriptionSegment>,
        quality_latency_ms: u64,
    ) -> FwResult<CorrectionDecision>
    
    /// Get running statistics for the adaptive controller.
    pub fn stats(&self) -> &CorrectionStats
    
    /// Get the correction rate (corrections / total windows).
    pub fn correction_rate(&self) -> f64
    
    /// Get mean WER across all windows.
    pub fn mean_wer(&self) -> f64
    
    /// Get all corrections for evidence export.
    pub fn corrections(&self) -> &[CorrectionEvent]
    
    /// Get a specific partial by seq.
    pub fn get_partial(&self, seq: u64) -> Option<&PartialTranscript>
    
    /// Check if all registered partials have been resolved.
    pub fn all_resolved(&self) -> bool
}

DECISION ALGORITHM (submit_quality_result):
1. Find the PartialTranscript for this window_id
2. If not found, return FwError::InvalidRequest (quality result without matching partial)
3. Compute CorrectionDrift::compute(partial.segments, quality_segments)
4. If always_correct OR drift exceeds any tolerance threshold:
   a. Set partial.status = Retracted
   b. Create CorrectionEvent
   c. Update stats (corrections_emitted++)
   d. Return CorrectionDecision::Correct
5. Else:
   a. Set partial.status = Confirmed
   b. Update stats (confirmations_emitted++)
   c. Return CorrectionDecision::Confirm

TOLERANCE DESIGN RATIONALE:
- max_wer=0.1 means: if more than 10% of words are wrong, correct it
- max_confidence_delta=0.15 means: if confidence differs by more than 15%, trust the quality model
- always_correct=true is for evaluation mode (measure how often fast model is wrong)
- These thresholds are configurable per-run, not hardcoded, because optimal thresholds depend on the model pair

DEPENDS ON: scs.1 (core types), scs.2 (robot events for emission)

title: Design SpeculationWindowController with alien-artifact engineering contract
description:
PHASE 3 ADAPTIVE INTELLIGENCE -- The alien-artifact controller that adaptively tunes the speculation window size based on correction evidence.

FILE: src/speculation.rs (extend)

WHY:
The optimal speculation window size is unknowable at compile time. It depends on:
- Audio quality (noisy audio needs larger windows for context)
- Model pair quality gap (tiny vs large has bigger gap than small vs medium)
- Speech rate (fast speech packs more words per ms)
- Domain (medical dictation vs casual conversation)

A fixed window size is always wrong for some inputs. The SpeculationWindowController observes correction rates and adaptively adjusts.

ALIEN-ARTIFACT ENGINEERING CONTRACT (per AGENTS.md):
Every adaptive controller must include:
1. Explicit state space
2. Explicit actions
3. Loss matrix
4. Posterior/confidence terms
5. Calibration metric
6. Deterministic fallback trigger
7. Evidence ledger artifact

HERE IS THE CONTRACT:

1. STATE SPACE:
   S = { correction_rate: f64, mean_wer: f64, window_count: u64, current_window_ms: u64 }
   - correction_rate in [0.0, 1.0]: fraction of windows that needed correction
   - mean_wer in [0.0, 1.0]: average WER across corrections
   - window_count: total windows processed (confidence indicator)
   - current_window_ms: current window size

2. ACTIONS:
   A = { Shrink(delta_ms), Hold, Grow(delta_ms) }
   - Shrink: reduce window size by delta_ms (min 500ms step)
   - Hold: keep current window size
   - Grow: increase window size by delta_ms (max 2000ms step)

3. LOSS MATRIX:
   L(state, action) where:
   - Cost of unnecessary correction = latency_penalty * quality_model_latency
   - Cost of larger window = latency_penalty * (window_ms - min_window_ms) / 1000
   - Cost of missed correction = accuracy_penalty * mean_wer
   Weights: latency_penalty=1.0, accuracy_penalty=5.0 (accuracy matters more)

   If correction_rate > 0.3 AND mean_wer > 0.15: Grow (windows too small, corrections too frequent)
   If correction_rate < 0.05 AND window_count > 10: Shrink (windows too large, corrections rare)
   Else: Hold

4. POSTERIOR/CONFIDENCE:
   - Confidence = min(window_count / 20, 1.0) -- need at least 20 windows for full confidence
   - When confidence < 0.5, prefer Hold over Shrink/Grow (insufficient data)
   - Bayesian update: P(optimal_window | observed_corrections) modeled as Beta distribution
   - Prior: Beta(2, 2) (weakly informative, centered at 0.5 correction rate)

5. CALIBRATION METRIC:
   - Predicted correction rate (from posterior) vs actual correction rate
   - Brier score over rolling window of 20 decisions
   - If Brier > 0.25: controller is poorly calibrated, trigger fallback

6. DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK:
   - If window_count < 5: use initial_window_size (no adaptation)
   - If Brier > 0.25: revert to initial_window_size
   - If correction_rate > 0.8: force max_window_ms (almost everything needs correction)
   - If correction_rate == 0.0 for 20+ windows: force min_window_ms (models agree on everything)
   - Fallback is ALWAYS safe (larger windows are slower but never wrong)

7. EVIDENCE LEDGER:
   - Each decision is logged as a SpeculationControllerEntry:
     { decision_id, window_id, state_snapshot, action_taken, predicted_correction_rate,
       actual_correction_rate_so_far, brier_score, confidence, fallback_active, fallback_reason }
   - Appended to the run's evidence ledger via PipelineCx::record_evidence()

TYPES:

pub struct SpeculationWindowController {
    initial_window_ms: u64,
    current_window_ms: u64,
    min_window_ms: u64,
    max_window_ms: u64,
    step_ms: u64,                  // Adjustment step size
    state: ControllerState,
    posterior: BetaPosterior,
    calibration: CalibrationTracker,
    evidence: Vec<SpeculationControllerEntry>,
    fallback_active: bool,
    fallback_reason: Option<String>,
}

pub struct ControllerState {
    pub correction_rate: f64,
    pub mean_wer: f64,
    pub window_count: u64,
}

pub struct BetaPosterior {
    pub alpha: f64,  // Corrections observed + prior
    pub beta: f64,   // Confirmations observed + prior
}

pub enum ControllerAction {
    Shrink(u64),
    Hold,
    Grow(u64),
}

impl SpeculationWindowController {
    pub fn new(initial_window_ms: u64, min_ms: u64, max_ms: u64, step_ms: u64) -> Self
    pub fn observe(&mut self, decision: &CorrectionDecision, drift: &CorrectionDrift)
    pub fn recommend(&self) -> ControllerAction
    pub fn apply(&mut self) -> u64  // Returns new window size after applying recommendation
    pub fn is_fallback_active(&self) -> bool
    pub fn evidence(&self) -> &[SpeculationControllerEntry]
    pub fn current_window_ms(&self) -> u64
    pub fn confidence(&self) -> f64
}

title: Word timestamps via cross-attention DTW (real alignment)
description:
Word-level timestamps via cross-attention DTW (real alignment — replaces interpolation; also upgrades Align stage).

SPEC (port of whisper.cpp/openai dtw timestamps):
- During decode (A7) optionally record cross-attention weights of alignment heads. Alignment-head selection: whisper.cpp ships per-model head lists (e.g. tiny.en specific heads); ggml file does NOT contain them — embed the published per-model alignment-head tables (from whisper.cpp dtw_aheads presets) keyed by (n_text_layer, n_text_state, model name hint); fallback: top-half layers all heads (openai fallback).
- Pipeline: attn weights [heads, tokens, audio_frames] -> select text-token rows -> median-filter over audio axis (width 7) -> normalize per head (subtract mean/std) -> average heads -> cost matrix -> DTW (monotonic path) -> token boundary times at 0.02s resolution -> aggregate token times into word times (split on whitespace/punct using tokenizer byte groups).
- Feed result into: (a) WordTimestampParams path of native engine (replaces interpolated), (b) orchestrator Align stage: when backend == native and word timings present, execute_align uses REAL aligned boundaries instead of char-density heuristic (keep heuristic as fallback for bridge backends; report which path ran in align payload "method":"dtw_attention"|"char_density").
TESTS: DTW unit (synthetic monotonic cost matrices, known paths incl. edge cases single-token/single-frame); median filter unit; gated e2e: jfk tiny.en word timestamps — assert word count == transcript word count, times monotonic non-overlapping within segment bounds, "ask" (first occurrence) within [7.0, 9.5]s sanity window (verify against whisper-cli -ml 1 output once, store fixture).

title: native_engine/ggml.rs: whisper.cpp ggml .bin model parser (f32/f16)
description:
Implement src/native_engine/ggml.rs: parser for whisper.cpp ggml .bin model files.

SPEC (verified against real files 2026-06-04 — see epic body for layout):
- Read magic 0x67676d6c, 11 i32 hparams into WhisperHParams (derive n_audio_ctx etc.; ftype 0=f32, 1=f16 — error with FwError::Unsupported listing the ftype for quantized formats for now).
- Read mel filterbank (n_mel x n_fft_bins f32) into MelFilterbank { n_mel, n_fft_bins, data: Vec<f32> } — this is the SAME filterbank whisper.cpp uses, so our mel frontend inherits exact filter weights from the model file (no librosa reimplementation needed).
- Read vocab: n_vocab_in_file entries (i32 len + bytes) into Vec<Vec<u8>> (tokens are RAW BYTES, byte-level BPE already applied — decode = concat). When hparams.n_vocab > file vocab, synthesize specials by id exactly as whisper.cpp does (e.g. [_TT_N] placeholder names not needed for decode; we only need id->bytes for real text tokens and to KNOW special ids — see tokenizer bead).
- Tensor directory: loop until EOF: n_dims(i32) name_len(i32) ftype(i32) dims[n_dims](i32, ggml order = reversed row-major) name(bytes) then 32-byte alignment? VERIFY against whisper.cpp model loader (whisper.cpp aligns tensor data; confirm by parsing tiny.en fully and checking total bytes consumed == file size). Store map name -> TensorEntry { shape: Vec<usize>, dtype, byte_offset, byte_len } over an mmap-free Vec<u8> file read (file sizes up to 3GB; read whole file into Vec<u8> is acceptable for now; note alternative seek-based loading as TODO comment for memory bead A14).
- Provide dequant: f16 -> f32 conversion in pure safe Rust (bit manipulation or half crate via ft-core's re-export — prefer half through ft-core to avoid new direct dep).
- API: GgmlModel::load(path) -> { hparams, filters, vocab_tokens, tensors: HashMap<String, TensorEntry>, blob } plus fn tensor_f32(&self, name) -> FwResult<(Vec<usize>, Vec<f32>)>.
TESTS: parse tiny.en (gated on file presence at $FRANKEN_WHISPER_TEST_MODEL_DIR or ~/models/whisper/) asserting exact hparams (39M tiny.en: n_vocab 51864, n_audio_state 384, n_audio_layer 4, n_text_layer 4, n_mels 80), filterbank dims 80x201, vocab size, presence+shape of known tensors (encoder.conv1.weight [384,80,3], decoder.token_embedding.weight [51864,384]), full-file consumption (no trailing bytes), f16->f32 spot values finite and in sane range. Also a tiny synthetic in-memory ggml blob built by the test itself for hermetic CI coverage of the parser paths (header roundtrip, unsupported-ftype error).

title: native_engine/decode.rs: greedy decode loop, timestamp rules, 30s windowing
description:
Implement src/native_engine/decode.rs: greedy decoding loop, timestamp rules, 30s windowing/seek.

SPEC (port whisper.cpp greedy strategy, temperature 0 path first):
- Per window: tokens = sot_sequence(lang, task, timestamps_enabled) (+ optional prompt/prev-context tokens capped at n_text_ctx/2); loop: forward decoder step, apply logit filters IN ORDER: suppress blank at step0, suppress non-speech tokens, timestamp pairing rules (after a timestamp, next must be text or eot; timestamps monotonic; sum-of-timestamp-probs > max-text-prob forces timestamp — port whisper.cpp logic), then argmax; stop at eot or n_text_ctx limit; collect avg logprob + no_speech prob (from sot step logits at nosp token) for QC.
- Segment extraction: split token stream at timestamp pairs -> TranscriptionSegment { start_sec = window_offset + ts, end_sec, text = tokenizer.decode(text_tokens), confidence = exp(avg_logprob) clamped }; handle single-timestamp tail (open segment to window end).
- Windowing: seek = window_offset + last complete segment end (or full 30s if no timestamps); language: if model multilingual and lang None -> detect once on first window (forward sot step, argmax over lang tokens); en-only models skip.
- no_speech gate: if no_speech_prob > 0.6 AND avg_logprob < -1.0 -> emit no segments for window, advance full window (matches whisper defaults).
- Cancellation checkpoint between every decoder step (token-level responsiveness — this is the project's cancellation contract, better than bridge's process-kill granularity!). Temperature>0 fallback on low avg_logprob: STRETCH (separate follow-up bead if not reached).
- API: NativeWhisperModel::transcribe(samples_16k_mono: &[f32], params { language, translate, timestamps, max_initial_ts, n_threads, checkpoint }) -> FwResult<Vec<TranscriptionSegment>> + per-window stats for evidence ledger.
TESTS: hermetic logit-filter unit tests (synthetic logits exercising every rule incl. timestamp forcing); gated e2e: jfk.wav + tiny.en greedy == fixture text EXACTLY (deterministic at temp 0): "And so my fellow Americans ask not what your country can do for you ask what you can do for your country." (capture exact punctuation from whisper-cli run); multi-window test on 60s concatenated fixture (jfk repeated) asserting both windows produce segments and monotonic timestamps.
close_reason: Implemented src/native_engine/decode.rs: greedy/temp-0 port of whisper.cpp whisper_full_with_state. Full logit-filter suite (process_logits, cited line-by-line), no_speech_prob from first-forward softmax, avg_logprob, 30s windowing/seek in centiseconds, segment building from timestamp pairs incl. open-tail, no-speech/single-segment/single-ts-ending rules, multilingual lang auto-detect, prev-context prompt. LoadedModel/DecodeParams/WindowStats/DecodeOutput/transcribe_samples match the bd-hsbx contract. Fixtures committed (jfk.wav + jfk_tiny_reference.json). 30 tests pass incl. gated e2e: native engine reproduces whisper-cli tiny.en transcript EXACTLY, 2 segments, timestamps within 0.3s, deterministic, multi-window monotonic. clippy -D warnings + rustfmt clean.

title: Profile and optimize native word timestamp DTW vs whisper.cpp
description:
## Background
Word-level timestamps are a core real-world feature and the README says native pilots must match bridge word output within the 50 ms tolerance. Existing native-engine perf artifacts focus on encoder/decoder transcription and long-call throughput; they do not isolate the DTW word-timestamp path against `whisper.cpp -wt`.

## Scope
Build a head-to-head workload for native word timestamps vs `whisper.cpp` word timestamps over short, long-form, noisy, and multi-speaker fixtures. Profile the DTW path before changing code. Candidate one-lever families include request/window-scoped DTW scratch arenas, banded/cache-oblivious DTW layout, SIMD/vectorized attention aggregation, or branchless word grouping. Implement only if the measured score is >= 2.0.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparator: `whisper.cpp` with word timestamp flags equivalent to franken's `WordTimestampParams`. Franken comparator: native `DecodeParams { word_timestamps: true }` through the same conformance corpus.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard section 5.10 region-based memory: request/window DTW scratch reset, only if allocations are top-5.
- Graveyard section 7.2 cache-oblivious layout: DTW matrix/cache behavior, only if cache misses dominate.
- Graveyard section 8.2 vectorized execution: batch attention/head aggregation with selection-like slices.
- Extreme optimization: one lever, golden word-timing conformance, re-profile.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: word-boundary or timestamp drift. Fallback trigger: any text mismatch, segment drift beyond 50 ms, word timestamp drift above agreed cap, or less than 3% p95 wall/RSS gain. All regressions must be added to docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

## Validation
Artifacts: p50/p95/p99, RSS, CPU profile, allocation profile if arena is considered, native-vs-`whisper.cpp` segment and word timing comparison, golden output hash, and ledger row.

## Success Criteria
A measured native-vs-original ratio for word timestamps on realistic fixtures, with either a kept >=3% win and green conformance or an explicit negative-evidence closeout.

title: P1 perf: token-level speculative decoding (draft model) — amortize the DRAM-bound decode (realistic-long-audio limiter)
description:
MEASURED gap: on realistic decode-heavy long audio the franken margin is DECODE-bound (multi-window e2e 1.12x vs single-window 1.34x; franken decode ~1.07x = parity with whisper.cpp, bd-6qih). WHY (DRAM-bound): each autoregressive token (m=1) streams ~342MB of f16 decoder weights from DRAM — 105M layer params (4 layers x [self+cross attn 4x1280^2 + mlp 2x1280x5120]) + 66M tied logits [51865x1280] — exceeding cache, re-streamed every token at the ~88 GB/s ceiling (DuskFinch) = ~3.9 ms/token. whisper.cpp pays the same => parity. No single-token kernel tweak beats a bandwidth floor.

LEVER (DIFFERENT primitive): token-level speculative decoding. A small draft model (e.g. tiny.en for large-v3-turbo) proposes K tokens; the target verifies all K in ONE batched (m=K) forward, reading the 342MB weights once for K tokens => ~Kx less target weight-bandwidth for accepted tokens. Greedy verification is BIT-IDENTICAL to greedy target decoding (accepts only tokens the target would emit) => conformance preserved. Projected ~2-3x decode speedup at ~70-90% acceptance, lifting realistic decode-heavy e2e well above the current 1.12x.

DISTINCT from existing speculation work: src/speculation.rs + bd-3vhz (long-form window scheduler) + bd-kdg7 (streaming TTFT) are WINDOW/STREAMING-level (fast model emits early, slow confirms a window). This is TOKEN-level within a single decode.

SCOPE: needs draft-model load + acceptance loop + dual KV-cache in src/native_engine/decode.rs + decoder.rs. Conformance gate: bit-exact greedy parity vs current greedy decode + WER<=0.10 vs whisper.cpp. Evidence + rationale in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md (2026-06-29 cc entry). Filed by AGENT_NAME=cc.

title: Benchmark and optimize real codec normalization vs ffmpeg plus whisper.cpp
description:
## Background
`franken_whisper` should dominate real-world non-WAV input handling because common formats decode in-process while `whisper.cpp` typically needs ffmpeg normalization. Current README figures list small normalization estimates, but there is no original-vs-franken ratio ledger across realistic MP3/AAC/FLAC/OGG/video workloads.

## Scope
Build a codec corpus covering clean speech, long-form speech, stereo/mono, VBR MP3/AAC, FLAC, OGG/Vorbis, and video fallback. Measure built-in normalization plus native transcription against an original `ffmpeg -> whisper.cpp` flow. Profile before changes. Candidate one-lever families: vectorized/branchless resampler, chunked decode buffers, fewer copies, reusable per-run sample buffers, or process/syscall elimination. Do not touch ASR kernels in this bead.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparator: `ffmpeg` normalization into `whisper.cpp` on the same final 16 kHz mono WAV contract. Franken comparator: built-in decoder path, with forced ffmpeg fallback as a control.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard section 8.2 vectorized execution: batch sample conversion/resampling over cache-sized slices.
- Graveyard section 5.10 region-based memory: per-normalization scratch reuse if allocation profile supports it.
- Graveyard section 0.10 benchmark standard: p95/p99 and RSS, not mean-only.
- Profiling skill: include syscall/process profile to separate subprocess overhead from decode work.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: audio drift changes transcript quality. Safe mode: compare normalized WAV hashes when expected identical, and otherwise compare audio invariants plus transcript conformance. Fallback trigger: audio invariant failure, transcript drift, or less than 3% p95 improvement.

## Validation
Required artifacts: per-codec p50/p95/p99, RSS/user CPU, syscall/process counts, normalized-audio hash or invariant report, transcript conformance, original-vs-franken ratio row, and negative-evidence update for abandoned levers.

## Success Criteria
Either a kept measured win over `ffmpeg -> whisper.cpp` on at least one common non-WAV workload, or a precise negative-evidence report identifying why built-in normalization is already at floor.
close_reason: Measured SampleBuffer reuse at 0.970x median with overlapping intervals; reverted and ledgered precise floor

title: native_engine/tokenizer.rs: whisper BPE decode + special-token map
description:
Implement src/native_engine/tokenizer.rs: whisper token decode + special-token map (pure Rust).

SPEC:
- Decode: token id -> raw bytes from ggml vocab (A1); concatenate; String::from_utf8_lossy at segment boundaries only (tokens can split UTF-8 chars — accumulate bytes per segment then convert ONCE).
- Special ids: replicate whisper.cpp derivation from vocab size. For multilingual v3 (n_vocab 51866): eot=50257, sot=50258, lang base=50259 (..50358, 100 langs), translate=50359, transcribe=50360, solm=50361, prev=50362, nosp=50363, not=50364 (no_timestamps), timestamp_begin=50365. For English-only tiny.en (n_vocab 51864): eot=50256, sot=50257, lang base=50258? VERIFY against whisper.cpp source logic (vocab.is_multilingual() = n_vocab >= 51865; specials computed relative: token_eot = n_vocab_in_file - 1 +? ) — DO NOT GUESS: port the exact whisper.cpp id arithmetic (whisper.cpp: token_eot = vocab.n_vocab_in_file - 1 for...; confirm by decoding known sequences with whisper-cli -oj output token ids on jfk.wav and asserting our map agrees). title: BLOCKER (narrowed): franken model gates need models/wavs rch never syncs; 32-thread perf gates need a >=32-core worker. Pure-cargo franken benches now RUN remotely (see z1w4).
description:
PRECISE BLOCKER. Two distinct classes of franken_whisper keep-gate are currently unrunnable.

CLASS 1 -- MODEL GATES (transcript diff, WER, e2e wall-clock).
The ggml model dirs and *.wav fixtures are gitignored, so rch never syncs them to a worker. Every model-dependent bench (e2e_probe, encoder_window spans, PROBE_DUMP_TEXT transcript diff, WER vs whisper-cli) SKIPs or fails remotely. Pre-existing ledgered limitation (docs/PERF_LEDGER.md "Measurement infrastructure findings", item 2), NOT an rch fault.

CLASS 2 -- PURE-CARGO PERF GATES AT 32 THREADS (found 2026-07-10 by cc_fw).
Even a model-free, self-contained criterion/example bench cannot produce an admissible ratio, because no sampled rch worker can field the thread count under test. franken_whisper caps encoder rayon at 32 threads (project_encoder_thread_cap_win), and scheduling levers only manifest at that T. Sampled workers, all forcing T=32:
  vmi1264463  available_parallelism=8    -> 4x oversubscribed, NOT ADMISSIBLE
  ovh-a       available_parallelism=16   -> 2x oversubscribed, NOT ADMISSIBLE
  hz2         not captured               -> cannot be certified
`rch exec` exposes no --worker and no --min-cores flag, and picks workers non-deterministically, so retrying does not help.

MEASUREMENT RULES (both cost us real work; obey both):
(a) Ratios are NOT worker-invariant. An A/B split across TWO rch invocations is INVALID -- discard any such ratio (franken_networkx br-r37-c1-839yx). Correct substrate: BOTH arms in ONE binary and ONE rch invocation, registered in the same alternating criterion group / rotated per rep, so worker identity and drift cancel within the run. The old "stash ORIG, bench, pop, bench NEW" recipe is doubly forbidden: it assumes one machine AND uses git stash.
(b) Single-binary is necessary but NOT sufficient. The host must ALSO have available_parallelism >= the thread count under test, or rayon work-steals across the oversubscription and smears the effect. `sgemm_tile_shape_ab` now prints an explicit `PERF *** NOT ADMISSIBLE ***` verdict; never quote a run that emitted it.

WHY THERE IS NO FALLBACK.
- Local `cargo build/bench/test` suspended by owner: /data at 96% (90G free); 11 concurrent local cargo builds drained ~450GB/h.
- `rch exec -- maturin build` FAILS OPEN to a local build (no strict-remote flag): observed one offload at 18MB then a 179MB local release/ tree. maturin must not be run at all.

WHAT STILL WORKS: pure-cargo CORRECTNESS via `rch exec -- cargo test` (verified: 12/12 gemm on hz2, 3/3 sdpa on vmi1149989, 1/1 sdpa_poly_exp_setter on vmi1227854). Bit-exactness is host-independent, so BIT-EXACT levers can still be certified remotely -- they just cannot be *sized*.

CONSEQUENCE: only bit-exact levers whose value is already established by a pre-directive baseline can ship. Everything else PARKS with the patch under tests/artifacts/perf/ + the captured baseline + a blocker note.

CURRENTLY BLOCKS:
- bd-bcm7 (FT_SDPA_POLY_EXP default-on for large-v3-turbo). Class 1. Evidence supports it: WER gate PASSES 4/4 on turbo, byte-identical 3/4, and on the one diverging clip ON is strictly CLOSER to whisper.cpp (8.519 -> 7.778). tiny.en does NOT pass (track01 52.800 -> 53.600) and stays off. The setter it needed is LANDED (frankentorch 1fb80836). Only the turbo transcript diff remains.
- bd-sgemm-tile-shape-imbalance-kf1j (35 tiles on 32 threads). Class 2. Bit-exactness certified on 3 workers; perf number has nowhere to run.
- SDPA BR row-block sweep (bit-exact, 1.028-1.039x on the kernel): its sub-1% e2e effect must be settled with `perf` instructions-retired = a bench. Class 2.

UNBLOCK (any one):
(a) free disk headroom on the 5975WX box (32 physical cores) and run the gates there;
(b) teach rch to sync the model dir + fixture wavs (rsync allowlist overriding .gitignore) AND expose a worker-capability filter (--min-cores);
(c) run the gates on a host that already has the models and >=32 cores.

REPRO once unblocked:
  FRANKEN_WHISPER_MODEL_DIR=legacy_whispercpp/whisper.cpp/models \
  PROBE_DUMP_TEXT=1 e2e_probe large-v3-turbo tests/fixtures/native/jfk.wav 3   # +/- FT_SDPA_POLY_EXP=1
  plus sample_audio_files/example_audio_track_01.mp3 (long, multi-speaker)

title: PARKED: sgemm tile_shape load imbalance (35 tiles on 32 threads) — bit-exact, patch saved, needs a >=32-core box
description:
BIT-EXACT lever, patch prepared and validated (git apply --check OK at frankentorch 1fb80836), NOT applied.
Artifact: franken_whisper tests/artifacts/perf/20260710-sgemm-tile-shape/ (patch + baseline + blocker).
Harness: frankentorch crates/ft-kernel-cpu/examples/sgemm_tile_shape_ab.rs (e959c67e).

DEFECT (certain, no measurement needed): gemm::tile_shape picks p=floor(sqrt(T)), q=ceil(T/p), so p*q != T for many T. At T=32 that is 5x7 = 35 tiles on 32 threads -> a straggler wave of 3 tiles while 29 threads idle. T=32 is exactly franken_whisper encoder thread cap. T=64 -> 8x8 and T=16 -> 4x4 are already balanced.

BIT-EXACT (certified, host-independent): the balanced grid is bit-identical to the shipped path on all three large-v3-turbo linear shapes, verified on 3 independent rch workers (A==B and A==C full-array; fidelity guard B/A = 0.954-1.028x). => NO transcript/WER gate needed. Only a perf number is missing.

BASELINE (32-core Zen3 5975WX, 32 rayon threads, interleaved, rotated, min-of-9, cv<=5%, captured BEFORE the local-build directive):
  qkv/out 1.022x | fc1 0.958x (REGRESSES) | fc2 1.241x
  layer 49.52 -> 46.57 ms = 1.063x  => encoder 1.045x => e2e ~1.04x

THE CATCH: a uniform balanced grid is NOT a clean win. fc1 regresses 4%. The straggler count is not the only force -- more column blocks shrink the per-thread B re-stream (k*nb*4 bytes), which fc1 wants (B=26.2MB, n=5120) and fc2 does not (n=1280; at q=16 nb clamps to MIN_BLOCK_COLS=128, collapsing to 20 tiles and under-filling the pool). Grid sweep (bit-exact throughout):
        32x1    16x2    8x4     4x8     2x16
  qkv   0.881   0.943   1.016   1.001   0.972
  fc1   0.778   0.970   0.805   0.958   1.085
  fc2   0.947   1.066   1.086   1.111   1.063
=> The REAL lever is a B-bytes-aware choice among the divisor pairs of T (minimize k*nb subject to nb >= MIN_BLOCK_COLS and p*q tiles filling the pool), not naive tile-count balance. Unmeasured. Do not land the parked patch and claim 1.24x; its honest number is 1.063x on the layer and it costs fc1 4%.

BLOCKED BY bd-transcript-gate-unrunnable-xu9g. Perf A/B needs a host with available_parallelism >= 32. Sampled rch workers: vmi1264463=8, ovh-a=16, hz2=uncaptured. rch exec has no --worker/--min-cores flag. Local builds disk-forbidden.

UNBLOCK (any one): (a) free disk on the 5975WX and run `cargo run --release -p ft-kernel-cpu --example sgemm_tile_shape_ab`; (b) add an rch worker-capability filter; (c) run on any >=32-core host and paste the table. Then implement the B-bytes-aware selector and re-sweep.

Filed by cc_fw.
close_reason: Admissible T=32 A/B captured on thinkstation1 (64c, build-remote/run-local): naive 4x8 grid = bit-exact layer 1.089x (~1.056x e2e), fc1 does NOT regress here. Selector marginal (1.098x). Owner-flip of set_sgemm_tile_balanced default recommended. See franken_whisper ecadc9c / frankentorch bf5c5c4b. Blocker edge dropped: local 64-core box fields T=32 (build remote, run local).

comments.text:
RESOLVED (admissible, 2026-07-11, cc_fw). Measured on thinkstation1 (64 cores, available_parallelism=64>=32 => ADMISSIBLE), built remotely via rch (vmi1227854), run LOCALLY at T=32, single binary, ABBA order-rotated, min-of-25. Replica-faithful: real f32 path sgemm_2d_parallel reads B UNPACKED with stride n (== harness tiled()), and real-A(5x7)=3.68ms sits between swept 4x8/8x4.

Naive uniform 4x8 grid (already gated behind set_sgemm_tile_balanced, default OFF) = clean BIT-EXACT win on ALL 3 turbo shapes: qkv 1.008x, fc1 1.143x, fc2 1.126x => layer 1.089x => e2e ~1.056x. The 5975WX fc1 regression at 4x8 (0.958x) that parked this does NOT reproduce here — host-specific.

B-bytes-aware selector (largest divisor q<=T/2 with ceil(n/q)>=MIN_BLOCK_COLS) picks the per-shape optimum (fc1 2x16) but that is only 1.098x vs naive 1.089x (~0.8%, within ~1 cv) => NOT worth a shape-dependent policy on a shared shipped crate. Naive grid captures the win.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: GATE CORRECTION 2026-07-11 (cc_fw): the e2e ~1.056x I recorded is a grep-the-gate error. The admissible 1.089x LAYER win is real for ft_kernel_cpu::matmul_tensor_contiguous_f32, BUT the DEFAULT large-v3-turbo/tiny.en engine takes enc_attn_out_i8i32_for (encoder.rs:507-523, default-ON for calibrated models) which int8-quantizes q/k/v/fc1/fc2 (i7 maddubs) + attn.out (i8xi32) => 'yields 0 f32 GEMMs/layer'. enc_linear dispatches Some(w_i7)=>matmul_bias_i7; only the None fallback reaches matmul_tensor_contiguous_f32 -> sgemm_2d_parallel -> tile_shape. So the 32 encoder linears NEVER call the optimized fn by default. Only conv2 (k=3840, one f32 GEMM/window) still hits the tiler => true default-turbo impact ~0.1-0.3%, NOT 5.6%. RECOMMENDATION DOWNGRADED: do not flip set_sgemm_tile_balanced expecting a turbo e2e win; it helps only ENC_INT8-off + non-calibrated models. Bit-exactness + function-level 1.089x stand.

title: REOPENED: weight-stationary f16 GEMV tile — prior REJECT benched cross_attn_k/v, which stopped using gemv_f16_batch on 2026-07-02
description:
LEDGER-INTEGRITY REOPEN (cc_fw, 2026-07-10). The 2026-07-09 REJECT of a token-block weight-stationary tile for gemv_f16_batch_rows is INVALID: its stated consumer does not exist.

THE FALSE PREMISE. The row claims: "cross_attn_k/v.forward(encoder_out) at tq=1500 loads NO w_i8 (they only get .dequant_to_f32_if(cross_proj_f32_enabled()), DEFAULT OFF) => they route to the f16 batch (gemv_f16_batch -> gemv_f16_batch_rows)."
Reality: cross_proj_f32_enabled() is `const DEFAULT_ON: bool = true` (mod.rs:701), flipped default-ON by a674b49 on 2026-07-02 ("flip cross-proj f32 sgemm DEFAULT-ON - 2.25x now active"), SEVEN DAYS before the row was written. Its doc: "Route the per-window cross-K/V PROJECTIONS through dequant-once f32 tiled sgemm INSTEAD of the f16 batched GEMV." decoder.rs:671,679 hand cross-K/V to WeightMat::F32 => nn::matmul_bias. Cross-K/V therefore contributes 0% of gemv_f16_batch self-time. The reject was benched at the CROSS shape [1500,1280]x[1280,1280], which that kernel no longer sees.

THE REAL CONSUMER. gemv_f16_batch has exactly one production call site (decoder.rs:345; nn.rs:5558 is a unit test), reachable only by WeightMat::F16 linears at tq>1 with no w_i8. Per decoder.rs:312, mlp_2 (fc2) is deliberately excluded from the int8 batch path because it carries a w_i8_block copy -- "those stay on the f16 batch path". So the true consumer is fc2 AT PREFILL: tq = prompt length (single digits), k=5120, n=1280.

WHAT TO DO. Re-measure the weight-stationary token-block tile at the fc2-prefill shape, NOT the cross shape. Expect a small prize: prefill runs once per window, not per token. Same-binary A/B (both arms one binary, one rch invocation; flip via a setter, never an env var). Record the self-time.

ALSO CORRECTED (no revert needed): the LANDED dot_f16c_2col / M2col win (2026-07-09, byte-exact, default-on, 1.212x) attributes itself to "the ~2% e2e cross_kv span" via the same false premise. The kernel result stands (bit-for-bit identical); its E2E ATTRIBUTION does not. Its real beneficiary is fc2 prefill. Do not carry "~2% e2e cross_kv" forward as this lever payoff.

ALSO: the ledger self-contradicts here -- 2026-06-29 REJECTED dot_f16c_2col (-0.84%, p=0.14) on the same kernel that 2026-07-09 LANDED at 1.212x. Two rows, opposite verdicts, same primitive, neither citing the other. Resolve when the true consumer is benched.

Filed by cc_fw.
close_reason: REJECTED by measurement on the REAL fn at the REAL consumer (fc2 prefill), one binary, interleaved arms, bit-exact. All fc2 ratios (1.020-1.037x) lie inside the NULL CONTROL's own +2.0% bias (cv 36.8%, sign p=1.00/1.00/0.30); at tq=100 row-morsel is 1.13x FASTER (p=0.0074), so the proposed 4*tq>=inp gate would have REGRESSED it. cross-KV control 0.601x (p=0.0001) confirms both paths execute. The 12-24x weight re-stream is NOMINAL traffic: bands run concurrently on the same 13.1 MB weight, served from shared cache. Ceiling <0.7% e2e even at a 100% delta. Family retired. franken ca2edb2.

title: REOPENED: i7 rowblock coarsening + i7 bias specialization gate the TOP owned frame (~28% self-time on turbo); their ratios are substrate-invalid
description:
REOPENED 2026-07-10 (cc_fw) after an in-situ profile CORRECTED my own audit.

MY AUDIT WAS WRONG. I claimed these rows have "0% self-time in the default engine", citing enc_int8_enabled() = DEFAULT_ON:false and encoder.rs:483 ("Default off => all i7 fields stay None"). I quoted the comment on the FIRST branch of an if/else-if chain and never read past it. The THIRD branch is `else if super::enc_attn_out_i8i32_for(&model.hparams)` -- the landed DEFAULT quality-safe int8 encoder -- which builds attn_q_i7/attn_k_i7/attn_v_i7/mlp_fc_i7 and routes attn.out through the full-i8 i32-accumulate GEMM. calibrated_encoder_int8_model() matches large-v3-turbo AND tiny.en.

MEASURED IN-SITU (perf -F 299, prebuilt release-perf e2e_probe, large-v3-turbo, jfk x8, load amortized, NO build):
  dot_maddubs_i7_m2n4                     14.63% self
  matmul_bias_i7_quantized::{closure#0}    9.91%
  encoder::matmul_bias_i8::{closure#1}     2.74%   (attn.out i8xi32)
  quantize_act_i7::{closure#0}             0.88%
  => i7 int8 encoder GEMM = ~28.2% self-time. THE HOTTEST OWNED CODE IN THE ENGINE.
For comparison: external matrixmultiply sgemm 14.31%, SDPA 11.46%, rayon overhead 11.25%.

SO THESE ROWS GATE A ~28% FRAME, AND THEIR RATIOS ARE INADMISSIBLE. As the audit correctly found, both A/Bs ran the candidate and the legacy arm as TWO SEPARATE rch bench invocations with FW_I7_ROWBLOCK_MIN_LEN flipped between them ("candidate coarse split (default 8, hz2)" vs "legacy original split (=1, hz2)"). rch has no --worker flag and ratios are not worker-invariant, so a two-invocation A/B is invalid. The legacy arm own spread is +/-1.30 ms on 12.79 ms (cv ~10%). A do-not-retry row over a 28% frame cannot rest on that.

PREREQUISITE FOR ANY RE-MEASURE: FW_I7_ROWBLOCK_MIN_LEN is a OnceLock env read, so it CANNOT flip inside one binary. It needs a runtime setter, exactly like set_sdpa_poly_exp / set_sgemm_tile_balanced. Add the setter first; then bench both arms in ONE binary / ONE rch invocation, arms interleaved inside a single measured routine, black_box on inputs and full output, with a NULL CONTROL (arm vs itself) to calibrate the floor, and record self-time per arm.

franken_whisper now DOES bench remotely: RCH_CONFIG_DIR=<scratch copy with total_timeout_ms 600000 + excludes> RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1 RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo bench -p franken_whisper --bench <name>  (verified on hz2, disk flat).

LESSON: static reachability is only as good as the branch you stopped reading at. Read the whole else-if chain, and confirm with a profile. A profile caught this in one command.

All 1,920,000 output f32 bits matched (SHA256 6803c12d...). Null p10/median/p90 0.735093/0.977603/1.106995; candidate p10/median/p90 0.747692/0.879877/1.161498, only 4/21 wins. title: rch cannot sync franken_whisper (52GB tree): sync_to_remote times out at 30s; use RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 to fail closed
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-10 (cc_fw). Two consecutive attempts:
  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo bench -p franken_whisper --bench f16_batch_prefill
  -> WARN rch::transfer: sync_to_remote: retryable error on attempt 1/3: timed out after 30000ms
  -> [RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback (remote execution failed)   rc=1

ROOT CAUSE: the franken_whisper working tree is 52 GB (target 2.2G, legacy_whispercpp 1.7G, perf.data 736M, plus more). rsync cannot complete inside rch sync_to_remote 30s window. By contrast frankentorch is 11 GB with all deps in-tree and syncs+benches fine: every remote run this session landed there (hz2, vmi1149989, vmi1227854, ovh-a).

CRITICAL SAFETY FINDING: WITHOUT RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, rch logs "Remote execution failed: sync_to_remote timed out, running locally" and SILENTLY BUILDS LOCALLY (rch diagnose confirms "Strict remote: off"; config has enable_last_success_fallback = true). Under a disk constraint that is a fall-open that drains ~73 GB/hour. WITH the flag, rch errors instead: measured disk delta across both failed attempts was ~1 MB, no local build.

MANDATORY FORM for every build/bench/test:
  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo <subcommand> ...
(env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR is required because ~/.zshrc globally exports CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target, which makes rch bench artifact retrieval return ~0 bytes.)
NEVER run maturin build: rch does not intercept it and it fails open to a local build.

CONSEQUENCE: no pure-cargo bench of franken_whisper can run anywhere right now. frankentorch benches DO run. So only levers living in frankentorch, or bit-exact levers whose value is already established, can ship. Everything else parks under tests/artifacts/perf/.

BLOCKS: bd-f16-gemv-weight-stationary-reopen-ugyh (fc2-prefill scheduler lever, bit-exact, ~0.4% e2e, patch + bench parked at tests/artifacts/perf/20260710-f16-batch-prefill/).

UNBLOCK (any one):
(a) raise rch sync_to_remote timeout, or give rch an rsync exclude list for target/, legacy_whispercpp/, perf.data, *.wav, model dirs (this is the cheap fix -- the source tree is only ~12 MB);
(b) shrink the working tree (owner call; I delete nothing);
(c) run the bench on a host with disk headroom.

Filed by cc_fw.
close_reason: RESOLVED: franken_whisper benches remotely via an alternate rch config (RCH_CONFIG_DIR to a scratch copy; total_timeout_ms 30000->600000; exclude legacy_whispercpp/, perf.data, .rch-targets/, *.wav, *.mp3, sample_audio_files/).
